title: 1st Shift Production Specialist
content:
About Formlabs: 
 Do you want to change how the world creates?
 At Formlabs, we’re building the tools that make it possible for anyone to bring their ideas to life, from cutting-edge products to life-saving medical devices. Our 3D printing technology powers innovation at more than 50,000 industry leaders worldwide, including Apple, Google, Tesla, New Balance, and NASA. Together, we’re helping everyone design, prototype, and manufacture faster than ever before.
 We’re a team of hands-on builders, engineers, and innovators reinventing how the world makes physical things. If you’re ready to shape the future of fabrication, come build it with us.
 Your Impact: 
 This position (Production Specialist) is responsible for the preparation and completion of engineered resins manufacturing for photochemistry applications. A detailed breakdown of the different responsibilities associated with this position is defined below. The 1st shift hours are 7am - 3:30pm, Monday through Friday.
 What You’ll Do: 
 Ensure a reliable live inventory of raw materials, WIP, or completed batches in the areas under his/her responsibility. You will be moving chemicals from inventory to mixing tanks and emptying drums into tanks.
 Provide first hand support to Production on issues associated with the resins based on the actual process parameters that may result in significant downtime.
 Ensure compliance with all Spectra health and safety and local, state, and federal regulatory requirements.
 Responsible for creating, reviewing, submitting and completing the resin recipes required to accomplish the production schedules.
 Submit and complete all the sampling associated with the batching process so batches are fully approved before use.
 Ensure the effective utilization of raw materials in the batching area so minimal waste or obsolescence is avoided while accomplishing his/her duties.
 Responsible to follow and maintain all the documentation associated with his/her activities as defined in the Quality Management System.
 Address any potential equipment or batching process issues that may affect or delay the batching schedule.
 You: 
 Associates degree or High School degree with production experience.
 Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
 Solid problem-solving abilities.
 Self-motivated with the ability to work on an independent basis.
 Strong organizational and time management skills.
 We Offer: 
 Medical, Dental, Vision
 3% match of yearly salary for 401(k)
 EAP Program
 In-office catering 3x per week
 120 hours of PTO per year
 We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. 
 Even if you don't check every box, but see yourself contributing, please apply. Help us build an inclusive community that will change the face of 3D printing.
 Compensation: 
 At Formlabs, base pay is one part of our total compensation package and is determined within a range. Your base pay will depend on your skills, qualifications, experience, location and expected impact on the organization. 
 The hourly base pay range for this role is: $17.75 — $21 USD

title: 3D Digital Manufacturing Technician
content:
Do you want to change how the world creates?
 At Formlabs, we’re building the tools that make it possible for anyone to bring their ideas to life, from cutting-edge products to life-saving medical devices. Our 3D printing technology powers innovation at more than 50,000 industry leaders worldwide, including Apple, Google, Tesla, New Balance, and NASA. Together, we’re helping everyone design, prototype, and manufacture faster than ever before.
 We’re a team of hands-on builders, engineers, and innovators reinventing how the world makes physical things. If you’re ready to shape the future of fabrication, come build it with us.
 We are seeking a detail-oriented 3D Digital Manufacturing Technician to join our team and help lead and execute day to day operations related to preparing, slicing, and optimizing parts for additive manufacturing. Your expertise in print setup, orientation strategies, Design for Manufacturing (DFM), and troubleshooting will ensure consistently high-quality output and streamlined production workflows.
 Responsibilities: 
 Prepare and slice CAD models for various 3D printing technologies (including FDM, SLA, and SLS) using various slicing software.
 Optimize print orientation, support structures, and settings to maximize quality, efficiency, and material usage.
 Identify and communicate potential design improvements using DFM principles to enhance printability and reduce post-processing.
 Troubleshoot print setup and orientation issues, analyze failures, and implement effective solutions.
 Collaborate with the internal teams and external customers to ensure alignment on technical requirements and improvements.
 Provide occasional support for printer operation tasks, including setup, maintenance, troubleshooting, and monitoring.
 Serve as the main liaison for customer inquiries regarding orders, project status, and technical specifications, ensuring professional and timely communication.
 Required Skills & Experience: 
 Hands-on experience with slicing and print setup software (PreForm, Cura, Simplify3D, Magics, Netfabb, etc.).
 Solid understanding of additive manufacturing processes and materials, particularly around print orientation, support generation, and print settings.
 Familiarity with Design for Manufacturing (DFM) concepts, specifically for 3D printing.
 Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills for diagnosing and resolving printing issues.
 Ability to effectively collaborate with cross-functional teams.
 Preferred Qualifications: 
 Experience operating industrial and consumer 3D printers
 Basic proficiency with CAD software (SolidWorks, Fusion 360, Onshape, ect).
 Familiarity with programming or scripting languages (Python) for automating processes.

title: 3D Print Optimization Engineer
content:
A 3D printer is one of the most demanding machines you can build.
 Lasers, optics, precision motion, thermals, airflow, materials handling, chemistry, sensing, controls, and software all have to work at micron-scale precision, for thousands of layers, with almost no tolerance for error. Making that work reliably is an extraordinary engineering problem.
 That’s what we do.
 At Formlabs, we’re building 3D printers that are changing the way things get made. We have the smartest minds across every engineering discipline, and the technology they’re building is deployed at more than 50,000 industry leaders worldwide, including Apple, Google, Tesla, New Balance, and NASA.
 If you’re energized by the idea of making the impossible happen, come join us as a 3D Print Optimization Engineer.
 The Print Optimization Team takes on the challenge of optimizing the intersection of hardware, software, and materials to deliver industry leading print performance. We strive to make our SLA & SLS product line print parts as quickly, reliably, easily, accurately, and beautifully as possible. We are a collaborative team, with a diverse background, passionate about pushing the boundaries of print performance across our product lines.
 As a 3D Print Optimization Engineer you will be continuously using your problem solving skills to drive improved performance. 
 We are customer focused, and the first step of tackling the problem is understanding what the performance boost we are trying to achieve, and how many customers will benefit. Will customers be able to print parts faster? More reliability? Will they be easier to post-process, or print more accurately? 
 If you’re excited about process optimization, solving multi-disciplinary challenges, and bringing to market the best print performance possible, we want you as a 3D Print Optimization Engineer! 
 The Job: 
 Push the capabilities of our SLA & SLS 3D printing platforms
 Drive root cause analysis, considering mechanics, fluid dynamics, software, chemistry, optics, electronics, thermodynamics, and customer behavior
 Design efficient experiments that tease out underlying behavior in a complicated system of variables
 Tackle multi-disciplinary problems
 Develop and commercialize solutions that make a real and immediate impact on customer print performance
 You: 
 Are focused on the customer
 Have a strong sense of ownership with great attention to detail
 Are hands-on and willing to cross discipline boundaries to solve a problem
 Work autonomously and learn new skills to tackle objective
 B.S., M.S., or PhD in any science/engineering discipline (all are welcome)
 Bonus: 
 Coding experience, ideally python
 Experienced in computer-aided design (CAD)
 Understand material properties and characterization
 Participated in the release of a new product
 Our Perks & Benefits: 
 Robust equity program to build future wealth through RSUs 
 Comprehensive healthcare coverage (Medical, Dental, Vision) 
 401K matching and access to financial advisors 
 Generous paid Parental Leave (up to 16 weeks) 
 Tenure-based paid Sabbatical Leave (up to 6 weeks) 
 Flexible Out of Office Plan – Take time when you need it 
 Ample on-site parking & pre-tax commuter benefits 
 Healthy on-site lunches, snacks, beverages, & treats 
 Regular sponsored professional development opportunities 
 Many opt-in culture events across our diverse community 
 And of course… unlimited 3D prints 
 We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. 
 Even if you don't check every box, but see yourself contributing, please apply. Help us build an inclusive community that will change the face of 3D printing.
 Compensation: 
 Equity is a big part of the compensation package at Formlabs - every employee receives equity because everyone contributes to building the company. We have a lot of confidence in the products we’re building and the impact we’re making, and you should too.
 Base pay is the other part of our compensation package, and it is carefully determined based on your skills, experience, and expected impact. Equity and base pay combine to make up your total compensation package at Formlabs.
 The annual base pay range for this role is: $85,000 — $148,000 USD

title: 3D Print Production Associate
content:
Do you want to change how the world creates?
 At Formlabs, we’re building the tools that make it possible for anyone to bring their ideas to life, from cutting-edge products to life-saving medical devices. Our 3D printing technology powers innovation at more than 50,000 industry leaders worldwide, including Apple, Google, Tesla, New Balance, and NASA. Together, we’re helping everyone design, prototype, and manufacture faster than ever before.
 We’re a team of hands-on builders, engineers, and innovators reinventing how the world makes physical things. If you’re ready to shape the future of fabrication, come build it with us.
 Summary: 
 We’re looking for reliable, hands-on team members to help us keep our 3D printing production running smoothly. In this role, you’ll work on a production floor where we use advanced 3D printers to make parts for customers around the world . No experience with 3D printing is required—we’ll teach you everything you need to know. 
 Role Description: 
 As a 3D Print Production Associate , you’ll help run machines, finish printed parts, check for quality, and prepare products for shipment. You’ll play an important part in making sure orders are completed on time and done right. This is a full-time, hourly position at our high-tech facility, where you’ll have the opportunity to learn and rotate through several different hands-on production stations.
 Responsibilities: 
 Operate 3D printers and other production equipment (training provided)
 Clean, finish, inspect, and package printed parts
 Follow quality standards and safety procedures
 Stay organized and keep your work area clean
 Work with teammates and communicate clearly with supervisors
 Help meet daily production goals
 Requirements: 
 Prior experience in manufacturing, warehousing, or a similar role is helpful but not required
 Strong attention to detail and ability to follow instructions
 Able to work independently and efficiently after training
 Comfortable in a fast-paced environment and willing to jump in where needed
 Work Environment and Physical Demands: 
 Work in a manufacturing environment with exposure to machinery noise, temperature changes, and particulate materials.
 Ability to stand, walk, and work on the production floor for extended periods.
 Lift and move objects weighing up to 50 pounds as needed.
 Perks & Benefits: 
 Comprehensive Healthcare Benefits through UMR (leveraging United Healthcare Provider Network)
 Vision and Dental included
 FSA/HSA
 Full-time, hourly employees will accrue PTO hourly, beginning on their start date, up to a maximum of 3 weeks (120 hours) PTO per year.

 Unlimited 3D Printing

 Our Engineering Print Farm is where we print parts for the engineering team to use for prototyping and quality purposes. If you are excited to work with your hands, we want you to join the Form Team as an 3D Print Technician.

 Running our Formlabs 3D printers
 Work with a team of diverse scientists to design and execute experiments, characterize materials, and develop print settings
 Editing Python scripts for print modification
 3D scanning, file organization, and data reporting
 Assist in testing requirements, goals, and features 
 You: 
 Experience running various 3D printers
 Always have an eagle eye on the details – no bad print part would get past you
 Ability to edit Python scripts
 Excited to see (and drive) the entire print production process from start to finish (printing, washing, cleaning, packing, shipping parts, and more!)
 Very focused and can operate efficiently with minimal supervision
 Can smoothly navigate competing priorities, tight deadlines, and last minute projects
 A friendly communicator who can interface with all teams to get things done
 Can streamline our production process and meet weekly quotas
 Diligent about meeting weekly quotas and targets

 Your Impact: 
 Formlabs is looking for a Finance & Operations Staff to bridge our transactional finance operations and physical plant production. This role is designed for a systems-minded, highly organized professional who thrives at the intersection of accounting, data analysis, and manufacturing operations.
 In this role you will spend your time maintaining foundational transactional accuracy and driving inventory control, Bill of Materials maintenance (“BOM”), and workflow optimization.
 What You’ll Do: 
 1. Accounts Payable & Employee Expenses 
 High-Speed Transactional Processing: Accurately process vendor invoices, credit notes, and employee Travel & Expense (T&E) reimbursement claims.
 Dispute & Inquiry Management: Serve as the primary point of contact for vendor inquiries, reconciling outstanding balances and resolving processing blocks.

 Daily Performance Logging: Partner with the plant production team to gather and input daily manufacturing data including the material consumptions, general inventory adjustments into the ERP systems.
 Production Sheet Integrity: Audit daily logs for discrepancies, missing records, or timing lags to ensure the team is working with 100% accurate plant-floor data.

 BOM & Cost Maintenance: Support the maintenance of accurate Bills of Materials (BOMs) and item costs in the ERP, flagging structural discrepancies between planned and actual configurations.

 Data Reporting & SOPs: Assist managers by pulling and formatting variance reports to provide leadership with the clean data needed to make strategic decisions.

 Passione per la stampa 3D e le tecnologie emergenti
 Esperienza in un ambiente di startup in rapida crescita

 Indennità di trasferimento
 Lavoro ibrido
 Pranzo offerto in ufficio 3 giorni alla settimana
 Assicurazione sanitaria privata con Medicare (pacchetto Blue + copertura ospedaliera)
 Abbonamento mensile o trimestrale ai trasporti pubblici per Budapest

 Bevande e snack gratuiti in ufficio
 Abbonamento sportivo All You Can Move con un contributo mensile di 9.500 HUF

content:
IP Counsel 
 Department: Legal
Location: Somerville, MA (on-site)
 About Formlabs: 
 A 3D printer is one of the most demanding machines you can build.
 Lasers, optics, precision motion, thermals, airflow, materials handling, chemistry, sensing, controls, and software must all work at micron-scale precision, for thousands of layers, with almost no tolerance for error. Making that work reliably is an extraordinary engineering problem.
 That’s what we do.
 At Formlabs, we’re building 3D printers that are changing the way things get made. We have the smartest minds across every engineering discipline, and the technology they’re building is deployed at more than 50,000 industry leaders worldwide, including Apple, Google, Tesla, New Balance, and NASA.
 Your Impact: 
 This role owns our patent portfolio strategy by building metrics to inform a global approach. You'll work closely with R&D and inventors who create new technologies to guide our future growth. Additionally, we operate as a lean legal team, so you'll have an exciting opportunity to expand beyond IP and advise business leaders globally on other areas of law, such as corporate, commercial, employment, and general litigation matters. 
 What You'll Do: 
 Own patent portfolio value, not just volume: build the metrics and criteria that determine what Formlabs patents, maintains, or cuts, and track cost against actual competitive value.
 Set global patent strategy across the U.S. and internationally, weighing where protection is worth pursuing given Formlabs' cross-border risk.
 Draft, file, and prosecute patent applications with the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) and international patent offices, including the European Patent Office (EPO) and the China National Intellectual Property Administration (CNIPA).
 Run freedom-to-operate (FTO) analyses, patentability assessments, and portfolio risk reviews to keep Formlabs building on solid ground.
 Partner directly with R&D to catch patentable inventions early, before they're buried in a lab notebook.
 Manage outside counsel across prosecution, opinions, and any disputes, keeping cost and quality in check.
 Support IP litigation, opposition proceedings, and enforcement when they come up.
 Step outside the patent portfolio to pitch in on key manufacturing, vendor, and supplier agreements, as well as other strategic commercial contracts.
 Pick up other generalist legal matters as they surface, from trade compliance to general litigation support, so the legal team can work collaboratively and best support any area of the business that needs our help.

 J.D. and admission to at least one state bar, plus registration to practice before the USPTO (patent bar).
 Undergraduate degree in engineering, physics, mathematics, or a related technical field. You need to be able to read a claim chart and the underlying spec without a translator.
 Deep expertise in U.S. patent law, plus working knowledge of major international patent systems; experience with trademark and trade secret law.
 A track record in patent drafting, prosecution, and portfolio management, ideally where you can point to real decisions you made about what to file and what not to file.
 At least 3 years at a top-tier law firm focused on patent work.
 While you index on patent work, you’re excited about an expanded scope to learn to operate as a generalist, taking on whatever tasks the business requires. You thrive in an “every day is different” environment and enjoy the challenge of solving novel problems as they arise. 
 Comfortable working independently in a fast-moving, global company where you're juggling more than one live priority at a time.

title: Chief Engineer
content:
A 3D printer is one of the most demanding machines you can build.
 Lasers, optics, precision motion, thermals, airflow, materials handling, chemistry, sensing, controls, and software must all work at micron-scale precision across thousands of layers, with almost no tolerance for error. Making that work reliably is an extraordinary engineering problem.
 That’s what we do.
 At Formlabs, we’re building 3D printers that are changing the way things get made. We have the smartest minds across every engineering discipline, and the technology they’re building is deployed at more than 50,000 industry leaders worldwide, including Apple, Google, Tesla, New Balance, and NASA.
 Your Impact: 
 Our technical leads drive the decisions that make our products great. From the system level to the details of each subsystem, you will sit at the intersection of technical challenges and high-impact product design decisions. You will be the main technical leader who drives the overall design of a shipping product.
 What you’ll do: 
 Partner with the Product Team to define product-level performance goals, providing the technical perspective needed to ensure targets are ambitious, achievable, and grounded in sound engineering.
 Lead architectural down-selection across all engineering domains (mechanical, optical, electrical, etc.), identify technological risk, and output a performant, robust system architecture. 
 Champion shipping a great product. Ultimately, you’ll be responsible for the product's final performance. 
 Own technical readiness for any new technologies and ensure we’re ready to incorporate them into a product. 
 Work with domain experts to define subsystem requirements and interfaces. 
 Guide team members through the technical implementation. Help them frame technical problems in terms of customer value, make design decisions through engineering rigor and objective data, and think beyond purely technical solutions. 
 Identify program risks and keep the team focused on the most important work. 
 About you: 
 You’ve led the technical development of a complex electro-mechanical product.
 You are familiar with a broad range of technologies, including mechanical, electrical, thermal, optical, material science, motion control, and embedded code 
 You have demonstrated success across the entire product lifecycle, from initial concept development to high-volume manufacturing
 You are comfortable with a culture of healthy debate and can defend design decisions with objective data

title: Director, Embedded Systems
content:
About Formlabs: 
 To reinvent an industry, you have to build the best team. Join Formlabs to be part of our mission to build the tools that enable anyone to bring their ideas to life. 
 Each Formlabs printer is a precision machine —a seamless orchestration of optics, mechanics, and chemistry. Its intelligence is driven by the critical layer in between: the firmware interpreting sensor data, the electrical architecture linking subsystems, and the integration layer that transforms individual components into a reliable tool for surgeons, engineers, and manufacturers worldwide.
 This is our printer’s nervous system, and we are searching for the leader to own its evolution. 
 Norbert Wiener coined the term cybernetics at MIT in 1948 to capture the idea of control systems across artificial and biological systems, kicking off decades of progress in this area. Over time, it has been broken down into narrow professional disciplines, including high-level software, embedded software, digital hardware design, analog hardware design, and mechanical engineering. It’s time to reunite these fields to refocus on the goal - make systems flexible, robust, and intelligent.

 Ship amazing products that are loved by customers and make a dent in the universe by making it easier for people to go from an idea to a real thing.
 Scale a world-class cybernetics engineering team , leading embedded engineering, systems integration, and electrical engineering globally.

 Build the Brain. Create a modular architecture (main boards, chipsets, peripherals) that scales across our entire ecosystem.
 Iterate at Speed. Move from "what if" to a working prototype faster than anyone else in the industry.

 You've shipped complex electromechanical products to production in high-performance environments — you understand what changes when you go from prototype to 100,000 units in the field

 Are comfortable moving between analog and digital systems

content:

 Experience in the consumer electronics industry

title: Embedded Software Engineering Manager
content:
About Formlabs: 
 Do you want to change how the world creates?
 At Formlabs, we’re building tools that let anyone bring ideas to life, from cutting-edge products to life-saving medical devices. Our 3D printing technology powers innovation at more than 50,000 industry leaders worldwide, including Apple, Google, Tesla, New Balance, and NASA. Together, we’re helping everyone design, prototype, and manufacture faster than ever before.
 We’re a team of hands-on builders, engineers, and innovators reinventing how the world makes physical things. If you’re ready to shape the future of fabrication, come build it with us.
 Your Impact: 
 Firmware turns a Formlabs printer from a box of boards, motors, lasers, and sensors into a machine people trust for a 12-hour print. It runs on more than 130,000 printers in dental labs, hospitals, factories, and engineering teams, from the Form 4 and Form 4L to the Fuse 1+ and Fuse X1. As our Embedded Engineering Manager , you'll lead the embedded software team that writes it, across microcontrollers and embedded Linux. We're adding new printers over the next few years, so the platform you build now decides how fast each new machine comes up and how well it holds up in the field.
 What You’ll Do: 
 Own delivery of embedded firmware for current and upcoming printers: hit program milestones, set the quality bar, and decide with program leads what ships now and what waits.
 Stay hands-on. Review architecture and code, debug on target hardware next to your engineers, and write code when the team needs another pair of hands.
 Set direction for a shared embedded platform (drivers, communication stacks, RTOS and embedded Linux integration, bootloaders, firmware updates and build infrastructure) so each new printer reuses what works instead of starting over.
 Hire strong embedded engineers, coach them toward their best work, and deal with performance problems directly and early.
 Partner with electrical engineering, systems integration, mechanical and software teams from board bring-up through production, and trace field failures back to root cause.
 Build the test automation, CI, and static analysis that let the team ship firmware updates to a large installed base without breaking it.
 Question requirements and cut work that doesn't matter to customers, so the team spends its time on what does.
 About You: 
 Experienced embedded software engineer who has shipped production firmware in C and C++ for complex electromechanical products such as robots, consumer electronics, medical devices or industrial equipment.
 You've led a team of embedded or firmware engineers, including hiring and managing performance.
 You've taken multiple products from prototype to volume production and supported them after launch.
 You're comfortable working from bare-metal microcontrollers to embedded Linux and multicore processors, using Python for tooling and testing.
 You've brought up boards and peripherals yourself (ADC, PWM, SPI, I2C, CAN, Ethernet), can read a schematic, and debug with a scope and logic analyzer.
 You can profile and optimize firmware for performance, memory, and power, and diagnose problems across several connected controllers using logs and trace data.
 You make decisions with incomplete information, move quickly, and can explain how a technical call affects the customer.
 You communicate clearly with electrical, mechanical, and software engineers, as well as product and program leads.
 Bonus Skills: 
 Linux kernel experience, such as writing device drivers
 Firmware for motion control, lasers or optics, or thermal systems
 Over-the-air (OTA) updates and device security for connected products
 Supporting a large fleet of connected devices in the field
 MISRA C or other safety-critical coding standards
 Passion and experience in 3D printing
 Background in electronics or robotics
 Our Benefits & Perks: 
 Robust equity program to build future wealth through RSUs
 Comprehensive healthcare coverage (Medical, Dental, Vision)
 401K matching and access to financial advisors
 Generous paid Parental Leave (up to 16 weeks)
 Tenure-based paid Sabbatical Leave (up to 6 weeks)
 Flexible Out of Office Plan – Take time when you need it
 Ample on-site parking & pre-tax commuter benefits
 Healthy on-site lunches, snacks, beverages, & treats
 Regular sponsored professional development opportunities
 Many opt-in culture events across our diverse community
 And of course… unlimited 3D prints
 We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. 
 Even if you don't check every box, but see yourself contributing, please apply. Help us build an inclusive community that will change the face of 3D printing.
 Compensation: 
 Equity is a big part of the compensation package at Formlabs - every employee receives equity because everyone contributes to building the company. We have a lot of confidence in the products we’re building and the impact we’re making, and you should too.
 Base pay is the other part of our compensation package, and it is carefully determined based on your skills, experience, and expected impact. Equity and base pay combine to make up your total compensation package at Formlabs.
 The annual base pay range for this role is: $170,000 — $250,000 USD

Formlabs participates in approximately 20 trade shows annually, ranging from smaller, 12sqm booths to large-format exhibits of over 200sqm, while continuously bringing new products and applications to market. You will independently define and execute event programs, collaborate across functions to achieve clear objectives, and continuously improve how our experiential marketing efforts support the business.
 The Job: 
 Own a portfolio of various trade shows, from 12sqm to 200+sqm
 Develop and execute plans to achieve event objectives, ensuring milestones are met and outcomes are delivered
 Lead end-to-end event planning and execution, including pre/post-event campaigns, staffing, booth management, and internal enablement for demos and presentations
 Collaborate with the design and marketing teams to ensure event presence effectively represents the brand and showcases our growing product portfolio
 Manage budgets, contracts, vendors, and logistics, optimizing spend and operational efficiency across multiple event formats
 Serve as a visible brand ambassador, building relationships with customers, partners, and prospects onsite
 Gather and analyze event performance insights, using learnings to continuously improve formats, messaging, and attendee experience
 Collaborate across Sales, Product, Design, and Marketing teams, providing recommendations and influencing decisions to maximize event impact
 Responsible for ordering and tracking event inventory including collateral, giveaways, etc.
 Travel as needed (~25% of the time) to attend events, oversee execution, and support onsite teams - mostly within Europe

 Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Communications, or a related discipline
 5+ years of experience in event marketing, including owning and executing complex B2B trade show and event programs
 Proven experience managing multi-event portfolios with booths ranging from small to large-format, including planning, execution, and reporting
 Experience supporting product launches and evolving product portfolios through events, ensuring effective market positioning
 Strong project management skills, highly organized, and able to manage multiple projects, resources, budgets, and onsite personnel under tight deadlines
 Excellent communication skills - written, oral, and cross-functional collaboration, including partnering effectively with Sales, Product, and Marketing teams
 Data and metric-driven, with the ability to draw insights from event and marketing data to optimize outcomes
 Creative, innovative, and proactive - able to identify new opportunities and think outside the box to improve event experiences

 Own a portfolio of various trade shows, from 12sqm to 200+sqm

 Collaborate with the design and marketing teams to ensure event presence effectively represents the brand and showcases our growing product portfolio
 Manage budgets, contracts, vendors, and logistics, optimizing spend and operational efficiency across multiple event formats
 Serve as a visible brand ambassador, building relationships with customers, partners, and prospects onsite

 Collaborate across Sales, Product, Design, and Marketing teams, providing recommendations and influencing decisions to maximize event impact

 2. Inventory Production Data Entry & Integrity 
 Daily Performance Logging: Partner with the plant production team to gather and input daily manufacturing data including the material consumptions, general inventory adjustments into the ERP systems.
 Production Sheet Integrity: Audit daily logs for discrepancies, missing records, or timing lags to ensure the team is working with 100% accurate plant-floor data.
 3. Inventory Management, Costing & BOM Maintenance 
 BOM & Cost Maintenance: Support the maintenance of accurate Bills of Materials (BOMs) and item costs in the ERP, flagging structural discrepancies between planned and actual configurations.
 Physical & Systemic Inventory Audits: Coordinate periodically inventory reconciliations, and research inventory counting variances.
 4. Process Optimization & Analytical Support 
 Continuous Improvement Execution: Actively look for small, daily efficiencies. Partner with leadership to identify manual bottlenecks on both the accounting and plant sides.
 Data Reporting & SOPs: Assist managers by pulling and formatting variance reports to provide leadership with the clean data needed to make strategic decisions.
 About You: 
 You are energized by both office finance work and factory-floor operations. 
 You enjoy working across teams (from accounting managers to production line workers) to close process loops.

title: Finance Systems Engineer
content:
Join Formlabs if you want to bring ground-breaking professional 3D printers to the desktop of every designer, engineer, researcher, and artist in the world.
 The Finance Systems team owns the enterprise systems used to record, process, and report financial data across Formlabs. We're looking for a Finance Systems Engineer who is equally comfortable writing code to automate and interconnect our finance stack and administering those systems day-to-day — owning the configuration, access, and operational health that keep NetSuite and Coupa running as a compliant, efficient source of truth.
 This is a hands-on role for someone who wants to both build (scripting, integrations, automation) and operate (privileged administration, BaU configuration, security). If you're as happy shipping a SuiteScript integration as you are provisioning a role, tuning an approval workflow, or debugging a failed PO sync, this is the role for you.
 Build & Integrate 
 Design, develop, and ship customizations and integrations across NetSuite, Coupa, and related financial systems (such as Adaptive, Avalara, or future custom-built tools) 
 Build and maintain integrations between finance systems and the wider landscape- Shopify, Salesforce, the data warehouse, and middleware/iPaaS — using REST/SOAP APIs, webhooks, and event-driven patterns.
 Automate reconciliations, data syncs, and reporting pipelines so that procurement, invoicing, sales, GL, and revenue data flow accurately across platforms in near real time.
 Write SQL and saved searches to power reporting that pulls from multiple sources and aligns with finance and business needs.
 Apply modern engineering practices- version control, code review, testing, and clear documentation- to deliver maintainable, well-documented solutions.
 Administer & Operate 
 Serve as a privileged administrator for NetSuite and Coupa, owning day-to-day system health, configuration, and change management.
 Manage user provisioning and deprovisioning, roles, permissions, and periodic access/security reviews to enforce least-privilege and support audit and audit and internal controls.
 Configure and maintain custom fields, records, forms, workflows, approval routing, and notifications as business processes evolve.
 Own saved searches, reports, dashboards, and KPIs; keep the reporting layer accurate and self-serve for finance stakeholders.
 Procurement approval chains and limits, content and account groups, supplier onboarding/SIM, and PO/invoice/expense configuration.
 Manage sandbox refreshes, release-preview and version testing, feature enablement, and bundle/SuiteApp management.
 Support period closes by maintaining subsidiary, tax, and entity configuration, and by monitoring integration error queues, audit logs, and data integrity across systems.
 Own license and subscription management, and act as the first line of triage for system issues, partnering with vendors and internal teams to resolve them.
 You: 
 A university degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, or equivalent practical experience.
 5+ years in finance systems engineering, ERP administration, or systems integration.
 Hands-on, demonstrable experience with NetSuite (both SuiteScript development and administration) and Coupa .
 Proven ability to manage system integrations using APIs and/or middleware tools.
 Ability to write SQL from scratch and comfort with reporting and data-warehouse concepts.
 Strong understanding of finance, procurement, and accounting workflows.
 A pragmatic problem-solver with excellent communication skills, willing to wear many hats and jump in wherever needed to deliver outcomes.
 Bonus Points: 
 NetSuite certifications (SuiteFoundation, Administrator, or SuiteScript Developer) and/or Coupa administration experience.
 Experience with additional finance/business systems (Salesforce, Shopify, Avalara/AvaTax, or similar) and iPaaS middleware.
 Ability to effectively leverage AI coding and tooling.
 Experience in a fast-paced, high-growth company that manufactures and sells physical products.

 Estamos em busca de profissionais dedicados e proativos para nos ajudar a manter nossa produção de impressão 3D funcionando perfeitamente. Neste cargo, você trabalhará no chão de fábrica, onde usamos impressoras 3D avançadas para fabricar peças para clientes do mundo todo.  As an FP&A Analyst, you’ll partner closely with leaders across the business to bring analytical rigor and clear financial insight to our operations. You’ll be a financial business partner to executives, own the financial model behind our inventory & COGS, drive automated reporting using SQL, develop gross margin and pricing recommendations across our printers, consumables, and services, and support corporate Treasury operations to keep our global subsidiaries well-funded. It’s a hands-on role with broad exposure across the company — ideal for someone who wants to deeply understand how products are designed, built, and brought to market.

 Partner directly with executive leaders across the company to monitor performance-to-budget across all programs.
 Lead data analytics projects from start to finish: Partner with leaders in Finance, Sales, Marketing, Product, Engineering, and Supply Chain to define problems, develop analysis plans, and deliver data-driven recommendations.
 Build and maintain financial models, for example, inventory and COGS forecasts grounded in unit economics and go-to-market assumptions for new products in the pipeline.

 What are the purchasing patterns of our customers? How does customer behavior differ by industry segment and use case?
 Develop and automate reporting: Build and maintain automated dashboards and reports that provide a clear, ongoing view of business performance for stakeholders.

 Act as the primary point of contact for resolving sync errors, ensuring that 'stuck' orders are identified and cleared within 24 hours.
 About You: 
 Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain or a related field; equivalent operational experience will also be considered.
 Solid understanding of order-to-cash cycles and basic warehouse operations (receiving, put-away, picking, and shipping).
 Exceptional organizational skills and the ability to multitask in a fast-paced environment where priorities can shift hourly.
 Strong communication skills, with the ability to provide clear, concise updates to both internal teams and external 3PL partners.
 A proactive, "figure-it-out" attitude with a commitment to high-quality execution and customer satisfaction.
 Bonus Skills: 
 Basic proficiency in Excel for data entry and simple report generation.
 Experience using Shopify, NetSuite, or common Warehouse Management Systems (WMS).
 Familiarity with regional carrier networks and basic domestic shipping regulations.
 Experience in a fulfillment, warehouse, or logistics coordination role, ideally within a high-growth e-commerce environment.

 Supplier sourcing, qualification, and negotiation processes.

 Have a technical or engineering background.

 Leadership experience and exposure to project management. 
 Eagerness to learn and adapt to new challenges.

 Manufacturing and procurement experience 
 Advanced use of Microsoft Excel 
 Product development experience 
 Familiarity with part inspection and corrective action, i.e. Quality Control 
 Experience with the manufacturing technologies used to make our printer parts: injection molding, machining, sheet metal stamping, bending, and forming, SMT etc.

title: Growth Marketing Lead, Form Now
content:
About Formlabs: 
 Do you want to change how the world creates?
 At Formlabs, we’re building the tools that make it possible for anyone to bring their ideas to life, from cutting-edge products to life-saving medical devices. Our 3D printing technology powers innovation at more than 50,000 industry leaders worldwide, including Apple, Google, Tesla, New Balance, and NASA. Together, we’re helping everyone design, prototype, and manufacture faster than ever before.
 We’re a team of hands-on builders, engineers, and innovators reinventing how the world makes physical things. If you’re ready to shape the future of fabrication, come build it with us.
 About Form Now 
 Form Now is a startup within Formlabs, backed by a small, fast-moving team of about 20 people. It's the next step in furthering Formlabs' mission: giving anyone, from individual builders to engineering teams, access to high-quality 3D printing without owning a printer. Users upload a model, choose from high quality materials, and Formlabs handles production, bridging the gap between idea and reality without the upfront cost of a machine. As the sole marketer for this business, you'll have full ownership of a marketing function and the challenge of scaling it from the ground up.
 Your Impact: 
 We're looking for a Marketing Generalist to own growth for Form Now end to end. We need someone who can wear many hats, from working on customer acquisition, to launching and iterating quickly on new campaigns. You'll need to be strong analytically, comfortable running email, events, and LinkedIn outreach, and willing to try channels you haven't touched before. You'll work directly with leadership to connect what the product can do with how we message and sell it to new customers.
 Breadth matters more than depth here. We'd rather have someone who can move fast across five channels than someone who's only ever gone deep on one.
 What You’ll Do: 
 Use analytics to identify where Form Now should grow next: which customer segments, which channels, and which campaigns are actually working
 Own campaign effectiveness end to end: set up email and LinkedIn campaigns, run them, and measure what drove results
 Independently plan and execute events as a channel for reaching new B2B customers, from small businesses to medium and large accounts
 Connect Form Now's product roadmap to marketing: turn what the product does into positioning and messaging that lands with buyers
 Pull together campaign analysis, competitive tracking, and channel experiments into a coherent growth plan you own end to end
 Make A/B testing and fast iteration a habit rather than an occasional exercise; ship, measure, adjust, repeat
 Write and manage customer-facing copy and email, from acquisition sequences to lifecycle messaging
 Use AI tools, including Claude, as a daily part of the job to move faster on research, campaign builds, and analysis
 About You: 
 2-10 years of B2B marketing or growth experience; slope and grit matter more than years
 A track record of taking on projects solo, from concept through execution, and knowing how you measured success
 Comfortable being customer-facing when the job calls for it
 Strong analytically: you can build a manageable tracking system, read your own campaign data, and act on it without waiting for someone else to hand you a dashboard
 Have run or set up events independently
 Growth mindset: you're not precious about the channel you know best and you'll try new approaches quickly
 High energy and not afraid to be scrappy; a startup-within-a-startup environment means undefined problems and few guardrails
 Use AI tools fluently in your daily work, held to the same quality bar as your own
 Bonus Skills: 
 B2B experience specifically
 Experience with data analytics and visualization tools (GBQ/SQL, DataStudio/Looker, etc.)
 Comfortable with copywriting and customer marketing, even if it's not your primary strength
 You've built your own tools, whether that's a scraper for a prospect list, an automation that stitches two tools together, or a landing page you shipped without waiting for design.

 Robust equity program to build future wealth through RSUs
 Comprehensive healthcare coverage (Medical, Dental, Vision)
 401K matching and access to financial advisors
 Generous paid Parental Leave (up to 16 weeks)
 Tenure-based paid Sabbatical Leave (up to 6 weeks)

 Healthy on-site lunches, snacks, beverages, & treats

 Base pay is the other part of our compensation package, and it is carefully determined based on your skills, experience, and expected impact. Equity and base pay combine to make up your total compensation package at Formlabs.

title: Head of Cybernetics
content:
About Formlabs: 
 To reinvent an industry, you have to build the best team. Join Formlabs to be part of our mission to build the tools that enable anyone to bring their ideas to life. 
 Each Formlabs printer is a precision machine —a seamless orchestration of optics, mechanics, and chemistry. Its intelligence is driven by the critical layer in between: the firmware interpreting sensor data, the electrical architecture linking subsystems, and the integration layer that transforms individual components into a reliable tool for surgeons, engineers, and manufacturers worldwide.
 This is our printer’s nervous system, and we are searching for the leader to own its evolution. 
 Norbert Wiener coined the term cybernetics at MIT in 1948 to capture the idea of control systems across artificial and biological systems, kicking off decades of progress in this area. Over time, it has been broken down into narrow professional disciplines, including high-level software, embedded software, digital hardware design, analog hardware design, and mechanical engineering. It’s time to reunite these fields to refocus on the goal - make systems flexible, robust, and intelligent.
 What You’ll Do: 
 Ship amazing products that are loved by customers and make a dent in the universe by making it easier for people to go from an idea to a real thing.
 Scale a world-class cybernetics engineering team , leading embedded engineering, systems integration, and electrical engineering globally. 
 Solve for Performance . Drive the embedded and electrical breakthroughs that enable our printers to do what others think is impossible.
 Build the Brain. Create a modular architecture (main boards, chipsets, peripherals) that scales across our entire ecosystem.
 Iterate at Speed. Move from "what if" to a working prototype faster than anyone else in the industry.
 About You: 
 You've shipped complex electromechanical products to production in high-performance environments — you understand what changes when you go from prototype to 100,000 units in the field
 You have built high-performance teams. 
 You are impatient and want to ship great products quickly.
 You are customer-obsessed , with a deep focus on the business to ensure we are building the right solutions for our customers 
 You dive deep into technical details across engineering and physics domains.
 Bonus Skills : 
 Passion and experience in 3D printing 
 Entrepreneurial experience that taught you what it takes to scale a business
 Our Benefits & Perks: 
 Robust equity program to build future wealth through RSUs
 Comprehensive healthcare coverage (Medical, Dental, Vision)
 401K matching and access to financial advisors
 Generous paid Parental Leave (up to 16 weeks)
 Tenure-based paid Sabbatical Leave (up to 6 weeks)
 Flexible Out of Office Plan – Take time when you need it
 Ample on-site parking & pre-tax commuter benefits
 Healthy on-site lunches, snacks, beverages, & treats
 Regularly sponsored professional development opportunities
 Many opt-in culture events across our diverse community
 And of course… unlimited 3D prints
 We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. 
 Even if you don't check every box, but see yourself contributing, please apply. Help us build an inclusive community that will change the face of 3D printing.
 Compensation: 
 Equity is a big part of the compensation package at Formlabs - every employee receives equity because everyone contributes to building the company. We have a lot of confidence in the products we’re building and the impact we’re making, and you should too.
 Base pay is the other part of our compensation package, and it is carefully determined based on your skills, experience, and expected impact. Equity and base pay combine to make up your total compensation package at Formlabs.
 The annual base pay range for this role is: $200,000 — $300,000 USD

title: Head of Hardware Product - SLS
content:
About Formlabs: 
 Do you want to change how the world creates?
 At Formlabs, we’re building the tools that make it possible for anyone to bring their ideas to life, from cutting-edge products to life-saving medical devices. Our 3D printing technology powers innovation at more than 50,000 industry leaders worldwide, including Apple, Google, Tesla, New Balance, and NASA. Together, we’re helping everyone design, prototype, and manufacture faster than ever before.
 We’re a team of hands-on builders, engineers, and innovators reinventing how the world makes physical things. If you’re ready to shape the future of fabrication, come build it with us.
 The Opportunity: 
 We are looking for an exceptional hardware product leader to own and grow our SLS hardware business, and to be the architect of what comes next. Reporting directly to the CPO, you’ll step into an established business with a strong foundation and an exciting new chapter to shape. The role is becoming available as our current leader moves to take on new responsibilities within our growing R&D organization.
 This isn't your typical product management role. You will operate with the autonomy of a startup founder, backed by the resources, brand, and manufacturing capability of a scaled company. You'll lead major hardware programs from concept to launch, lead a team of product managers, define roadmap strategy for an entire product line, and make the calls that determine how Formlabs competes and succeeds in additive manufacturing.
 We're looking for someone who has done hard things: Founded a company, shipped physical products, and competed seriously to be #1. A background in 3D printing is not required. We build complex systems that span materials, robotics, and software, with a GTM engine that spans prosumer through industrial sales. The successful candidate has technical ability to dive deep across domains, commercial sense to understand what customers want and how to make it work for the business, marketing chops to communicate a compelling vision, the data skills and customer obsession required to support an opinionated point of view, and strong leadership traits: drive, grit, and desire to win.
 Your Impact: 
 Your mandate is to define and drive the vision and strategy for the SLS business - identify where the market is going, build the roadmap to get there first, build the buy-in to execute across the organization, and lead the cross-functional teams that make it real. We value a bias for action, comfort with ambiguity, and deep ownership over outcomes. A successful leader has both a sharp understanding of what customers actually value, and a clear-eyed view of what's technically and commercially feasible, with the poise required to make challenging trade-offs required to build exceptional products, fast. 
 What You’ll Do: 
 Own the full hardware product roadmap for the SLS business, across discovery, definition, development, and delivery, supported by strong customer insights and market analysis, through program execution and launch.
 Lead multi-disciplinary teams across engineering, design, manufacturing, and commercial functions. You are the connective tissue that ensures we ship exceptional products that customers love and drive strong financial results for the business.
 Make high-stakes decisions on product positioning, hardware architecture tradeoffs, and go-to-market timing. Understand the customer value behind every major call, not just the technical rationale.
 Represent the voice of the customer inside the building, and the voice of the product in front of customers. Be the person who actually knows how our hardware gets used, why, and by whom.
 Partner deeply with engineering leadership: know enough to pressure-test what's feasible, identify what smells wrong, and find solutions from adjacent domains when the obvious path is blocked.
 Operate with urgency. You don't wait for permission. You don't confuse activity with progress. You find a way.
 About You: 
 We hire divergent people. Founders, athletes, people who've done something genuinely hard and come out the other side knowing what they're made of. If your path has been linear and comfortable, this is probably not the right fit.
 You've built real hardware - multiple generation products, major programs, or an entire company. You know what it takes to ship hardware that works reliably for the customer and for the business.
 You have previously led a significant business or founded a hardware venture. The experience of owning vision,P&L, roadmap, results, and team simultaneously is not new to you.
 You aren't just a "product person." You understand how roadmap strategy, technical hardware decisions, customer acquisition, and manufacturing operations must work in harmony.
 You possess the builder's mindset: the creativity to imagine what is possible, and the ability and the willingness to do whatever it takes to make it real - whether that's pitching a major customer, reviewing an engineering spec, or personally unblocking a production issue.
 You've gotten results without enough money, time, or people. You don't fold when the work gets difficult.
 Bonus Skills: 
 Experience in 3D printing, additive manufacturing, or adjacent physical product categories. (Having domain knowledge does not make you good at this job - but not having it will slow you down.)
 Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, or a related technical discipline.
 MBA or equivalent experience owning a P&L or leading a high-growth GTM motion.
 Familiarity with hardware manufacturing standards and compliance (ISO, medical, aerospace, etc.).
 Strong proficiency with data - exploration, extracting signal from noise, sizing markets, and presenting findings in a way that drives decisions.

title: Head of Information Technology (IT)
content:
Join Formlabs if you want to bring ground-breaking professional 3D printers to the desktop of every designer, engineer, researcher, and artist in the world.
 As the Head of Information Technology (IT) at Formlabs, you will own the foundation the whole company runs on: our global network, on-premise servers, endpoints, IT service desk, identity and access, and the security program that protects Formlabs and our customers’ data. This is a single, combined leadership role — where you will lead as a player-coach.
 You will lead a global team of 7 spanning network administration, systems administration, help desk, and cybersecurity, and support offices in Somerville, Germany, Budapest, and Shenzhen.
 You will join the Systems team, which enables every Formlabs team with enterprise applications, infrastructure, data, AI, and security. You will report to the CIO.
 This role is based in our Somerville, MA office and is an onsite role. 
 The Job: 
 Team Leadership: Lead, coach, and develop a team of 7 across network, systems, help desk, and cybersecurity. Set clear priorities, build strong technical leadership within the team, and grow the team’s automation and scripting skills.
 Network & Connectivity: Own our Cisco Meraki estate across four countries — SD-WAN and site-to-site VPN, firewalls, segmentation, Wi-Fi, ISP circuits, cloud VPN tunnels, remote access, and the specific connectivity and compliance requirements of operating in China.
 Strategy & Roadmap: Define and drive a combined infrastructure and security roadmap that balances reliability, risk, cost, and user experience — and explain it in business terms to the CIO, CFO, and company leadership. 
 Servers & Resilience: Own on-premise compute (Proxmox) and the services that run on it — lifecycle, patching, monitoring, backup and tested restores, and disaster recovery — and make deliberate decisions about what stays on-prem versus moves to cloud or SaaS.
 Security Program: Own Formlabs’ cybersecurity program end to end: policy, risk register, vulnerability and patch management, endpoint protection, email and SaaS security, logging, data loss prevention, and incident detection, response runbooks, and exercises.
 Staffing Model & Services: Provide leadership on how the team is staffed and which services it relies on — deciding what to build in-house versus source from managed service and security partners — and hold those partners accountable to clear scope and SLAs.
 Identity & Access: Own the joiner/mover/leaver process, SSO and MFA, privileged and break-glass access, and admin hygiene across Google Workspace and core SaaS — with the evidence trail auditors expect.
 IT Service Desk & Endpoints: Ensure a fast, friendly, measurable help desk for ~800 employees — ticket SLAs, onboarding/offboarding, laptop lifecycle and MDM, conference room and A/V, and site support — and personally own the hardest escalations.
 Automation & AI: Replace manual, repeatable work with automation and AI-assisted workflows across provisioning, monitoring, ticket triage, and reporting, so the team scales with the company.
 Vendors & Budget: Own the infrastructure and security vendor portfolio and budget — contracts, renewals, licensing, and hardware refresh plans — and make clear build/buy/partner tradeoffs.
 Documentation & Continuity: Maintain current diagrams, inventories, runbooks, and on-call/escalation coverage so no system depends on a single person’s knowledge.
 You: 
 Experience: 8+ years in IT infrastructure and/or security, including 2+ years leading teams, ideally in a mid-sized (500–2,000 person) company with multiple international sites.
 Network & Systems Depth: Hands-on expertise in enterprise networking (routing, VPN, firewalls, segmentation, Wi-Fi) and server virtualization; you can review a firewall rule set or a backup design yourself.
 Security Leadership: Practical experience building or running a security program at a company without a large dedicated security team — including EDR, identity, vulnerability management, and incident response.

title: Head of Intellectual Property
content:
IP Counsel 
 Department: Legal
Location: Somerville, MA (on-site)
 About Formlabs: 
 A 3D printer is one of the most demanding machines you can build.
 Lasers, optics, precision motion, thermals, airflow, materials handling, chemistry, sensing, controls, and software must all work at micron-scale precision, for thousands of layers, with almost no tolerance for error. Making that work reliably is an extraordinary engineering problem.
 That’s what we do.
 At Formlabs, we’re building 3D printers that are changing the way things get made. We have the smartest minds across every engineering discipline, and the technology they’re building is deployed at more than 50,000 industry leaders worldwide, including Apple, Google, Tesla, New Balance, and NASA.
 Your Impact: 
 This role owns our patent portfolio strategy by building metrics to inform a global approach. You'll work closely with R&D and inventors who create new technologies to guide our future growth. Additionally, we operate as a lean legal team, so you'll have an exciting opportunity to expand beyond IP and advise business leaders globally on other areas of law, such as corporate, commercial, employment, and general litigation matters. 
 What You'll Do: 
 Own patent portfolio value, not just volume: build the metrics and criteria that determine what Formlabs patents, maintains, or cuts, and track cost against actual competitive value.
 Set global patent strategy across the U.S. and internationally, weighing where protection is worth pursuing given Formlabs' cross-border risk.
 Draft, file, and prosecute patent applications with the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) and international patent offices, including the European Patent Office (EPO) and the China National Intellectual Property Administration (CNIPA).
 Run freedom-to-operate (FTO) analyses, patentability assessments, and portfolio risk reviews to keep Formlabs building on solid ground.
 Partner directly with R&D to catch patentable inventions early, before they're buried in a lab notebook.
 Manage outside counsel across prosecution, opinions, and any disputes, keeping cost and quality in check.
 Support IP litigation, opposition proceedings, and enforcement when they come up.
 Step outside the patent portfolio to pitch in on key manufacturing, vendor, and supplier agreements, as well as other strategic commercial contracts.
 Pick up other generalist legal matters as they surface, from trade compliance to general litigation support, so the legal team can work collaboratively and best support any area of the business that needs our help.
 About You: 
 J.D. and admission to at least one state bar, plus registration to practice before the USPTO (patent bar).
 Undergraduate degree in engineering, physics, mathematics, or a related technical field. You need to be able to read a claim chart and the underlying spec without a translator.
 Deep expertise in U.S. patent law, plus working knowledge of major international patent systems; experience with trademark and trade secret law.
 A track record in patent drafting, prosecution, and portfolio management, ideally where you can point to real decisions you made about what to file and what not to file.
 At least 3 years at a top-tier law firm focused on patent work.
 While you index on patent work, you’re excited about an expanded scope to learn to operate as a generalist, taking on whatever tasks the business requires. You thrive in an “every day is different” environment and enjoy the challenge of solving novel problems as they arise. 
 Comfortable working independently in a fast-moving, global company where you're juggling more than one live priority at a time.

This is a single, combined leadership role — where you will lead as a player-coach.

 Team Leadership: Lead, coach, and develop a team of 7 across network, systems, help desk, and cybersecurity. Set clear priorities, build strong technical leadership within the team, and grow the team’s automation and scripting skills.
 Network & Connectivity: Own our Cisco Meraki estate across four countries — SD-WAN and site-to-site VPN, firewalls, segmentation, Wi-Fi, ISP circuits, cloud VPN tunnels, remote access, and the specific connectivity and compliance requirements of operating in China.
 Strategy & Roadmap: Define and drive a combined infrastructure and security roadmap that balances reliability, risk, cost, and user experience — and explain it in business terms to the CIO, CFO, and company leadership. 
 Servers & Resilience: Own on-premise compute (Proxmox) and the services that run on it — lifecycle, patching, monitoring, backup and tested restores, and disaster recovery — and make deliberate decisions about what stays on-prem versus moves to cloud or SaaS.
 Security Program: Own Formlabs’ cybersecurity program end to end: policy, risk register, vulnerability and patch management, endpoint protection, email and SaaS security, logging, data loss prevention, and incident detection, response runbooks, and exercises.
 Staffing Model & Services: Provide leadership on how the team is staffed and which services it relies on — deciding what to build in-house versus source from managed service and security partners — and hold those partners accountable to clear scope and SLAs.
 Identity & Access: Own the joiner/mover/leaver process, SSO and MFA, privileged and break-glass access, and admin hygiene across Google Workspace and core SaaS — with the evidence trail auditors expect.
 IT Service Desk & Endpoints: Ensure a fast, friendly, measurable help desk for ~800 employees — ticket SLAs, onboarding/offboarding, laptop lifecycle and MDM, conference room and A/V, and site support — and personally own the hardest escalations.
 Automation & AI: Replace manual, repeatable work with automation and AI-assisted workflows across provisioning, monitoring, ticket triage, and reporting, so the team scales with the company.
 Vendors & Budget: Own the infrastructure and security vendor portfolio and budget — contracts, renewals, licensing, and hardware refresh plans — and make clear build/buy/partner tradeoffs.
 Documentation & Continuity: Maintain current diagrams, inventories, runbooks, and on-call/escalation coverage so no system depends on a single person’s knowledge.

 Experience: 8+ years in IT infrastructure and/or security, including 2+ years leading teams, ideally in a mid-sized (500–2,000 person) company with multiple international sites.
 Network & Systems Depth: Hands-on expertise in enterprise networking (routing, VPN, firewalls, segmentation, Wi-Fi) and server virtualization; you can review a firewall rule set or a backup design yourself.
 Security Leadership: Practical experience building or running a security program at a company without a large dedicated security team — including EDR, identity, vulnerability management, and incident response.

title: Lead Embedded Software Engineer
content:
About Formlabs: 
 Do you want to change how the world creates?
 At Formlabs, we’re building tools that let anyone bring ideas to life, from cutting-edge products to life-saving medical devices. Our 3D printing technology powers innovation at more than 50,000 industry leaders worldwide, including Apple, Google, Tesla, New Balance, and NASA. Together, we’re helping everyone design, prototype, and manufacture faster than ever before.
 We’re a team of hands-on builders, engineers, and innovators reinventing how the world makes physical things. If you’re ready to shape the future of fabrication, come build it with us.
 Your Impact: 
 Firmware turns a Formlabs printer from a box of boards, motors, lasers, and sensors into a machine people trust for a 12-hour print. It runs on more than 130,000 printers in dental labs, hospitals, factories, and engineering teams, from the Form 4 and Form 4L to the Fuse 1+ and Fuse X1. As our Embedded Engineering Manager , you'll lead the embedded software team that writes it, across microcontrollers and embedded Linux. We're adding new printers over the next few years, so the platform you build now decides how fast each new machine comes up and how well it holds up in the field.
 What You’ll Do: 
 Own delivery of embedded firmware for current and upcoming printers: hit program milestones, set the quality bar, and decide with program leads what ships now and what waits.
 Stay hands-on. Review architecture and code, debug on target hardware next to your engineers, and write code when the team needs another pair of hands.
 Set direction for a shared embedded platform (drivers, communication stacks, RTOS and embedded Linux integration, bootloaders, firmware updates and build infrastructure) so each new printer reuses what works instead of starting over.
 Hire strong embedded engineers, coach them toward their best work, and deal with performance problems directly and early.
 Partner with electrical engineering, systems integration, mechanical and software teams from board bring-up through production, and trace field failures back to root cause.
 Build the test automation, CI, and static analysis that let the team ship firmware updates to a large installed base without breaking it.
 Question requirements and cut work that doesn't matter to customers, so the team spends its time on what does.
 About You: 
 Experienced embedded software engineer who has shipped production firmware in C and C++ for complex electromechanical products such as robots, consumer electronics, medical devices or industrial equipment.
 You've led a team of embedded or firmware engineers, including hiring and managing performance.
 You've taken multiple products from prototype to volume production and supported them after launch.
 You're comfortable working from bare-metal microcontrollers to embedded Linux and multicore processors, using Python for tooling and testing.
 You've brought up boards and peripherals yourself (ADC, PWM, SPI, I2C, CAN, Ethernet), can read a schematic, and debug with a scope and logic analyzer.
 You can profile and optimize firmware for performance, memory, and power, and diagnose problems across several connected controllers using logs and trace data.
 You make decisions with incomplete information, move quickly, and can explain how a technical call affects the customer.
 You communicate clearly with electrical, mechanical, and software engineers, as well as product and program leads.
 Bonus Skills: 
 Linux kernel experience, such as writing device drivers
 Firmware for motion control, lasers or optics, or thermal systems
 Over-the-air (OTA) updates and device security for connected products
 Supporting a large fleet of connected devices in the field
 MISRA C or other safety-critical coding standards
 Passion and experience in 3D printing
 Background in electronics or robotics

 That’s what we do.
 At Formlabs, we’re building 3D printers that are changing the way things get made. We have the smartest minds across every engineering discipline, and the technology they’re building is deployed at more than 50,000 industry leaders worldwide, including Apple, Google, Tesla, New Balance, and NASA.
 If you’re energized by the idea of enabling employees to bring their (seemingly impossible) ideas to life, come join us as a Makerspace Fellow.
 The Job 
 Maintain printers and tools in Community SLA printing spaces: routine cleaning, inspections, tank and cartridge swaps, and first-line troubleshooting.
 Keep the Community SLA Print Farm and Makerspace stocked, safe, and organized (resin, consumables, PPE, IPA and waste handling, hand and power tools).
 Print parts for the Workplace Experience and Recruiting teams, from internal event pieces to giveaways for career fairs and candidate events.
 Design and maintain the signage, workflows, and documentation that guide any employee to print independently.
 Host office hours and intro sessions for first-time printers.
 Find ways to improve how the equipment and workspaces are set up for making.
 Update the Fellow handbook as you go, so the next Fellow starts stronger than you did.
 Spend 2-4 hours per week working on a personal design or engineering project that showcases a unique or technically complex use of Formlabs hardware, software, and/or materials. 
 You: 
 A hands-on maker: you’ve built, fixed, or printed something because you wanted to see it exist.
 Organized and reliable; you can own a recurring checklist and keep it current.
 Comfortable helping people across a wide range of technical backgrounds, from engineers to recruiters.
 Self-directed with minimal supervision, and quick to ask for help when you get stuck.
 3D printing experience with any technology (SLA or SLS a plus).
 Current undergraduate student.
 Bonus Skills (Optional): 
 CAD experience (Fusion, Onshape, SolidWorks, Blender, etc.)
 Experience in a makerspace, fab lab, school shop, or customer-facing role
 Graphic design or content creation (signage, social)
 Fellow Benefits & Perks: 
 Flexible schedule built around your classes
 Dedicated personal project time, plus materials
 Ample on-site parking & pre-tax commuter benefits
 Catered on-site lunches (3x per week), snacks, beverages, & treats
 Cohort-based social and professional development experience
 Many opt-in culture events across our diverse community
 And of course… unlimited 3D prints
 Compensation: 
 Interns at Formlabs are paid on a bi-weekly pay schedule. The pay range for this role will depend on your skills, qualifications, experience, location and expected impact on the organization. This is a salaried role, so you will always be paid based on the assumed 40 hours per week as a full-time intern. This position does not offer housing or relocation assistance. 
 The weekly pay range for this role is: $1,000 — $1,300 USD

title: Manufacturing Maintenance Technician
content:
To reinvent an industry, you have to build the best team. Join Formlabs if you want to bring groundbreaking professional 3D printers to the desktop of every designer, engineer, researcher, and artist in the world. 
 This position is responsible for assisting in providing support in maintenance, repair and support to assigned service calls to gain knowledge and skills for career development within Facility maintenance. Demonstrate the company’s core values of respect, honesty, integrity, diversity, inclusion, and safety. A detailed breakdown of the different responsibilities associated with this position is defined below. We have openings for both 1st shift and 2nd shift.
 Key Tasks and Responsibilities 
 Assist in performing various preventive maintenance tasks and procedures concerning buildings and equipment.
 Possess the ability to navigate and troubleshoot PLC's and related controls equipment.
 Develop skills for troubleshooting and repair of equipment.
 Assist in performing component replacement.
 Maintain an accurate and organized inventory of parts.
 Operate equipment, vehicles, powered industrial trucks, and aerial lifts safely.
 Perform routine building maintenance duties, including painting, minor electrical repairs, plumbing, carpentry, and heating and ventilation systems maintenance.
 Clean the interior of the building, as well as machinery and equipment, and exterior of the building
 Complete administrative duties, such as filling out forms and reporting maintenance statuses to supervisor.
 Comply with all safety and health regulations.
 Keep inventory of maintenance and cleaning supplies and equipment, and report needs to supervisor.
 Respond to emergency calls for maintenance and repairs.
 Diagnose and troubleshoot issues.
 Work with and maintain relationships with contracted vendors.
 Properly complete all repair, labor, parts purchasing and usage documentation in a timely fashion.
 Comply with all department and company policies and procedures.
 Physical demands include, but are not limited to, high aptitude for standing and walking endurance, lifting and carrying up to 50 pounds, pushing and pulling climbing ladders of various types, bending, squatting, and kneeling, and working in different temperatures inside and outside.
 Core Competencies 
 Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
 Solid problem-solving abilities.
 Self-motivated with the ability to work on an independent basis.
 Strong organizational and time management skills.
 Strong mechanical skills.
 Preferred Skills and Qualifications 
 Experience with troubleshooting PLC
 5+ years of relevant maintenance experience 
 What We Offer 
 Medical/dental/vision insurance 
 3% 401k match
 Company-provided lunch 3 days a week
 Unlimited access to 3d printing
 Education and Training 
 High School degree.
 Preferred Education 
 Bachelor's degree
 Compensation: 
 At Formlabs, base pay is one part of our total compensation package and is determined within a range. Your base pay will depend on your skills, qualifications, experience, location and expected impact on the organization. 
 The hourly base pay range for this role is: $27 — $33 USD
