title: Materials Manufacturing Innovation Engineer
content:
About Formlabs: 
 Do you want to change how the world creates? 
 At Formlabs, we’re building the tools that make it possible for anyone to bring their ideas to life, from cutting-edge products to life-saving medical devices. Our 3D printing technology powers innovation at more than 50,000 industry leaders worldwide, including Apple, Google, Tesla, New Balance, and NASA. Together, we’re helping everyone design, prototype, and manufacture faster than ever before. 
 We’re a team of hands-on builders, engineers, and innovators reinventing how the world makes physical things. If you’re ready to shape the future of fabrication, come build it with us. 
 Why this role 
 Most specialty materials are still made the way they have been for decades: weigh, mix in a tank, filter, fill. We think there’s a better way to make them, and we want you to invent it. 
 Our R&D team creates innovative materials that push the limits of 3D printing, and we need proven manufacturing processes to produce our materials at scale and bring them to market. This isn’t a traditional process engineering role. You won’t be tuning existing equipment or running scale-up checklists. You’ll invent what materials manufacturing looks like next: set up proof of concept pilot processes for new manufacturing technologies, design new mixing and dispersion approaches, and smart control systems that catch a bad lot before it happens. You’ll prototype it, prove it, and put it on the plant floor. 
 If you’ve ever looked at a production line, thought "there has to be a better way", and then built it, this is your job. 
 No 3D printing experience required. We need someone who understands how materials behave at scale and can’t stop thinking of better ways to make them. 
 You might currently be called: Manufacturing Technology Engineer, Advanced Manufacturing Engineer, R&D Engineer, Innovation Engineer, Research Engineer, Technology Development Engineer, or Process Development Engineer. 
 What you’ll own 
 An innovation roadmap for how Formlabs makes materials: where new technology could raise quality, cut cost, or let us make materials we can’t make today 
 New manufacturing approaches from idea to plant floor: concept, bench experiments, prototype equipment, pilot runs, and the business case to deploy 
 Co-invention with R&D, so new materials and the methods that make them are designed together from day one 
 Scouting existing technologies that will improve cost throughput quality and bringing the best ideas into Formlabs 
 Handing proven innovations to the plant team, with the documentation and training to run them 
 Proving out at least one new manufacturing technology at bench or pilot scale, with a clear case for production 
 About you 
 4+ years building new manufacturing technology in chemicals, coatings, adhesives, inks, pharma, advanced materials, or a similar field, in industry 
 A track record of introducing new manufacturing methods that has impacted product quality, cost or throughput 
 Strong grounding in the science of making materials: mixing, heat and mass transfer, and rheology of viscous or filled fluids 
 You move comfortably from first-principles thinking to a bench prototype to a pilot run 
 You use designed experiments and data to tell good ideas from great ones, and you can build the business case for the one worth deploying 
 Strong communication with cross-functional stakeholders 
 BS, MS, or PhD in chemical engineering, materials science, mechanical engineering, polymer science, or a related field 
 Bonus skills 
 Continuous manufacturing or process intensification 
 Inline sensors, process analytical technology (PAT), or chemometrics 
 Machine learning or AI applied to manufacturing data 
 UV-curable or other photoreactive materials 
 Polymer powder handling, for future SLS materials work 
 Modeling, automation, or data tools (Python, COMSOL, PLC/DCS)

title: Materials Program Manager
content:
About Formlabs: 
 A 3D printer is one of the most demanding machines you can build.
 Lasers, optics, precision motion, thermals, airflow, materials handling, chemistry, sensing, controls, and software all have to work at micron-scale precision, for thousands of layers, with almost no tolerance for error. Making that work reliably is an extraordinary engineering problem.
 That’s what we do.
 At Formlabs, we’re building 3D printers that are changing the way things get made. We have the smartest minds across every engineering discipline, and the technology they’re building is deployed at more than 50,000 industry leaders worldwide, including Apple, Google, Tesla, New Balance, and NASA.
 Your Impact: 
 Materials Program Managers at Formlabs usher in new technology from concept through production, partnering with the materials scientists and the product stakeholders to develop world-class 3D printing materials. They are the nexus between the internal teams, senior management, and external partners, coordinating all program activities from development through production ramp to product launch. 
 We look for people who are passionate about learning and taking on new challenges, care about shipping impactful products, and are interested in building strong collaborative relationships with external partners and internal teams.
 What You’ll Do: 
 Ship the best product as fast as possible 
 Manage the strategy, overall planning, execution and delivery of technically complex products from concept through production
 Monitor projects on an ongoing basis, evaluate progress/quality, and manage issue resolutions. Communicate status, issues, and key risks.
 Act as the link between the program teams, key stakeholders, and external partners, including frequent reporting to company leadership.
 Use disciplined project management methodology to define scope, develop program plans which deliver the program within cost and schedule
 Organize beta testing activities. Plan and coordinate the creation and implementation of externally facing technical documents
 Ensuring program closure - including post launch issue tracking and required documentation.
 About You: 
 5+ years of experience in an engineering or R&D environment, with demonstrated experience in project or program management.
 Understand how to bring product concepts from the lab to commercialization.
 Ability to apply technical knowledge to drive decision making, i.e. trade-off discussions and program strategy
 Strong organizational skills along with demonstrated ability to manage multiple projects and priorities simultaneously. 
 Outstanding verbal and written communication skills. Not afraid to speak up or pivot to a new direction when needed. 
 Self-starter and natural problem solver. Have a desire to increase the effectiveness of your teammates.
 Ability to work cross-functionally between product, engineering, production, and supply chain personnel. Experience communicating status and issues upward to product stakeholders and senior management. 
 Highly collaborative and results driven, constantly striving to improve schedule and program efficiency.

 Lasers, optics, precision motion, thermals, airflow, materials handling, chemistry, sensing, controls, and software all have to work at micron-scale precision, for thousands of layers, with almost no tolerance for error. Making that work reliably is an extraordinary engineering problem.
 That’s what we do.
 At Formlabs, we’re building 3D printers that are changing the way things get made. We have the smartest minds across every engineering discipline, and the technology they’re building is deployed at more than 50,000 industry leaders worldwide, including Apple, Google, Tesla, New Balance, and NASA.
 Materials development presents one of the greatest opportunities to innovate in 3D printing, unlocking new applications in different industries such as engineering, consumer, manufacturing, automotive and healthcare. Our materials science team works closely with product management, hardware and software teams to develop new materials that push the boundaries of what can be done with 3D printing.
 If you are a scientist or engineer with experience in polymer development who’s excited to break new ground in an industry that’s moving at lightning speed, we want you as a Materials Scientist .
 The Job: 
 Conduct research and develop world-class materials for 3D printing from initial lab explorations to validation and commercialization
 Collaborate with hardware and software engineers to ensure new and existing materials print on our hardware seamlessly and reliably
 Design and perform experiments, and use the results to inform and develop materials performance improvements
 Partner with product management, hardware, and software engineers to continuously improve our materials
 You: 
 A creative and resourceful problem-solver, balancing speed and scientific rigor in a dynamic environment
 Have solid understanding of the fundamentals of materials science and polymer development
 Passionate about testing and troubleshooting, not afraid to test hundreds of times
 Love to harness data; can design and conduct rigorous experiments to optimize materials
 Can work autonomously and take initiative to learn new skills to complete an objective
 Understand the value of good documentation
 Excited to collaborate with a diverse group of scientists and engineers
 B.S., M.S., or PhD in a relevant science or engineering field (all are welcome)
 Bonus Skills: 
 Experience developing materials for 3D printing, especially for SLA/DLP or SLS printers!
 3D CAD modeling
 Programming skills (Python, Matlab, SQL, etc)
 Our Perks: 
 Robust equity program to build future wealth through RSUs
 Comprehensive healthcare coverage (Medical, Dental, Vision)
 401K matching and access to financial advisors
 Generous paid Parental Leave (up to 16 weeks)
 Tenure-based paid Sabbatical Leave (up to 6 weeks)
 Flexible Out of Office Plan – Take time when you need it
 Ample on-site parking & pre-tax commuter benefits
 Healthy on-site lunches, snacks, beverages, & treats
 Regular sponsored professional development opportunities
 Many opt-in culture events across our diverse community
 And of course… unlimited 3D prints
 We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. 
 Even if you don't check every box, but see yourself contributing, please apply. Help us build an inclusive community that will change the face of 3D printing. 
 Compensation: 
 Equity is a big part of the compensation package at Formlabs - every employee receives equity because everyone contributes to building the company. We have a lot of confidence in the products we’re building and the impact we’re making, and you should too.
 Base pay is the other part of our compensation package, and it is carefully determined based on your skills, experience, and expected impact. Equity and base pay combine to make up your total compensation package at Formlabs.
 The annual base pay range for this role is: $75,000 — $142,000 USD

 What You’ll Do: 
 Design and optimize complex photopolymer formulations to push the boundaries of additive manufacturing.
 Lead the end-to-end transition of new materials from lab scale concept to commercial launch, supporting technology transfer and scale-up.
 Establish structure-process-property relationships through rigorous experimentation and analytical characterization to meet demanding product specifications.
 Learn about the 3D printing process and underlying hardware, and use that knowledge to inform formulation decisions and provide input to future hardware decisions.
 Collaborate cross-functionally with product management, hardware, and software teams to develop products that meet customer needs and work seamlessly on the Form 4 platform.
 About You: 
 BS, MS, or PhD in polymer science, chemical engineering, chemistry, materials science or a related field.
 Results-oriented and motivated by delivering products in a fast-paced R&D environment.
 Experience developing thermoset materials including epoxies, urethanes, or acrylates.
 Enjoys working hands-on in the lab conducting experiments and analyzing large data sets to drive decision making.
 Able to work autonomously and push projects forward with a high level of independence. 
 Track record of success including publication, IP generation, or product commercialization.
 Practices good documentation and can organize complex data, create SOPs, and write clear, detailed internal reports.
 Bonus Skills: 
 Familiarity with additive manufacturing technologies
 Programming and digital analysis (Python, JMP, MATLAB, Minitab etc)
 Experience with high performance polymers, composites, or elastomers

title: Mechanical Engineer - Entry Level
content:
A 3D printer is one of the most demanding machines you can build.
 Lasers, optics, precision motion, thermals, airflow, materials handling, chemistry, sensing, controls, and software all have to work at micron-scale precision, for thousands of layers, with almost no tolerance for error. Making that work reliably is an extraordinary engineering problem.
 That’s what we do.
 At Formlabs, we’re building 3D printers that are changing the way things get made. We have the smartest minds across every engineering discipline, and the technology they’re building is deployed at more than 50,000 industry leaders worldwide, including Apple, Google, Tesla, New Balance, and NASA.
 If you’re energized by the idea of making the impossible happen, come join us as a Mechanical Engineer.
 Include a portfolio with your application to show us what you can do. 
 The Job: 
 The job is to ship the best desktop 3D printers on the market:
 Prototype new mechanisms, from precision latches to revolutionary pumps and valves to surfaces measured in microns
 Test materials that push the boundaries of what 3D printing can do
 Research 3D printing challenges and rethink every subprocess to push technology forward
 Analyze, validate, and iterate on electro-mechanical systems
 Model everything from brackets to hinges to complex parts in CAD, creating well-specified, accurate drawings
 Partner with Global Sourcing and Manufacturing Teams to bring designs from prototype to mass production 
 Flex your global savvy by working with teams around the world, virtually and in-person
 Apply your knowledge of manufacturing techniques like injection molding and sheet metal fabrication to the world of 3D printing
 Solve customer problems by using your engineering skills to eliminate friction at every stage of their workflow
 You: 
 You can’t wait to build a precision tool that combines the power of injection molding with the beauty of the iPhone.
 You want to build a precision tool that is beautiful inside and out ( but don’t take our word for it )
 You know how to partner with people in any role with the genuine goal of getting work done and doing it well
 You love the gritty details of part design, material selection, and manufacturing techniques, because you know it’s important to commit to a vision and fail fast
 You craft elegant designs that function with efficiency and simplicity
 You work confidently in 3D CAD software (Solidworks/Onshape) to design components, produce drawings, and build assemblies
 You deeply understand the full product development cycle
 If you have Python skills, experience with contract manufacturers, know PLM or document control systems, or have a passion for industrial design, we want you to apply! 
 Our Perks & Benefits: 
 Unlimited 3D printing with any Formlabs material on any Formlabs printer
 An equity program that will let you build wealth through RSUs
 Healthcare coverage (medical, dental, vision) that includes a totally free employee-only plan, effective starting on your first day on the job
 401K matching with no vesting or tenure requirement
 Generous parental leave (fully paid up to 16 weeks)
 Flexible time off so you can take time when you need it
 Six-week fully paid sabbatical after hitting tenure milestones (with the option to take an additional six weeks after that)
 Free on-site parking & pre-tax commuter benefits
 Free on-site lunch, snacks, beverages, treats, beer kegs, and employee-favorite local coffee and espresso
 Self-driven professional development opportunities like conferences, trade shows, and hackathons
 One-of-a-kind activities and events like monthly socials, the annual weekend summer camp, a can’t-miss company hackathon, and lots of other social opportunities
 You don’t need to check every box to apply for a role. If you love working with hardware, spending time with smart people, solving hard problems, and winning, we want to hear from you. 
 We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

 Equity is a big part of the compensation package at Formlabs - every employee receives equity because everyone contributes to building the company. We have a lot of confidence in the products we’re building and the impact we’re making, and you should too.
 Base pay is the other part of our compensation package, and it is carefully determined based on your skills, experience, and expected impact. Equity and base pay combine to make up your total compensation package at Formlabs.

title: Mechanical Engineering Intern (Summer 2027)
content:
Do you want to change how the world creates?
 At Formlabs, we’re building the tools that make it possible for anyone to bring their ideas to life, from cutting-edge products to life-saving medical devices. Our 3D printing technology powers innovation at more than 50,000 industry leaders worldwide, including Apple, Google, Tesla, New Balance, and NASA. Together, we’re helping everyone design, prototype, and manufacture faster than ever before.
 We’re a team of hands-on builders, engineers, and innovators reinventing how the world makes physical things. If you’re ready to shape the future of fabrication, come build it with us.
 Your Impact: 
 Designing 3D printers is a cross-discipline experience where each individual contributes a portion of the overall knowledge required to bring a product to market. It seems like a daunting task from the outside; however, it can be broken down into smaller pieces that, when combined, result in a sophisticated device that embodies a lot of science, engineering, and manufacturing know-how. If you are passionate about hands-on engineering and rapid prototyping and are ready to tackle intriguing challenges on a real world product, we want you on our team as a Mechanical Engineering Intern. 
 Internship Term: Summer 2027 (May/June - August)
 Commitment: Full-time
 Location: Onsite in Somerville, MA
 Application Requirements: A portfolio of your previous engineering work/projects is required. View our Portfolio FAQ here! 
 The Job: 
 Design, assemble, test, and evaluate the performance of 3D printers.
 Participate in design reviews and help solve design, engineering, and manufacturing problems.
 Polish your time management and communication skills to increase your effectiveness as an engineer.
 Build prototype components and assemblies using our in-house facilities. 
 Put your CAD skills to work designing parts and assemblies, creating engineering drawings and learning about the importance of documentation control.
 Assist with direct communications to our vendors and suppliers to help overcome production challenges.
 You: 
 Have a desire to hone your skills and learn more about engineering design and the process of bringing products to market.
 Have worked with complex mechanical or electro-mechanical systems and want exposure to the inner workings of 3D printers.
 Have one-or-more of the following hands-on experiences:
 Lab research, member of a project team, prior internship or previous work experience
 Have an up to date resume and portfolio of your previous experience to highlight what you have learned and how you have applied that learning.
 Intern Benefits & Perks: 
 Flexible Out of Office Plan – take time when you need it
 Salaried bi-weekly pay schedule
 Ample on-site parking & pre-tax commuter benefits
 Catered on-site lunches (3x per week), snacks, beverages, & treats
 Cohort-based social and professional development experience for interns
 Many opt-in culture events across our diverse community
 And of course… unlimited 3D prints
 We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. 
 Even if you don't check every box, but see yourself contributing, please apply. Help us build an inclusive community that will change the face of 3D printing.
 Our Candidate AI Guidelines are available here . Please give them a read.
 Compensation: 
 Interns at Formlabs are paid on a bi-weekly pay schedule. The pay range for this role will depend on your skills, qualifications, experience, location and expected impact on the organization. This is a salaried role, so you will always be paid based on the assumed 40 hours per week as a full-time intern. This position does not offer housing or relocation assistance. 
 The weekly pay range for this role is: $1,575 — $1,950 USD

title: Mechanical Project Manager
content:
About Formlabs: 
 A 3D printer is one of the most demanding machines you can build.
 Lasers, optics, precision motion, thermals, airflow, materials handling, chemistry, sensing, controls, and software all have to work at micron-scale precision, for thousands of layers, with almost no tolerance for error. Making that work reliably is an extraordinary engineering problem.
 That’s what we do.
 At Formlabs, we’re building 3D printers that are changing the way things get made. We have the smartest minds across every engineering discipline, and the technology they’re building is deployed at more than 50,000 industry leaders worldwide, including Apple, Google, Tesla, New Balance, and NASA.
 Your Impact: 
 The Mechanical Project Manager makes sure our prototyping and development process is efficient and executed firmly. At Formlabs we’re constantly iterating on our products and building new prototypes. As the engineering project manager you’ll work with the mechanical engineering team and the engineering team broadly to bring these prototypes to life and once they’re built to make sure they’re being maintained and used effectively. You’ll also work closely with the mechanical engineering team to support the complexities of developing hardware such as managing BOMs, inventory and product configurations. This is a role that benefits from energizing your peers and has high visibility as your results are our highly coveted prototype products.
 What You’ll Do: 
 Be the glue to pull disparate teams together to hit key milestones and goals through the product development process
 Manage (in conjunction with the G$ team) the Bill of Materials for our products making sure it is up to date and usable for ordering, cost analysis and useful for tracking development status.
 Push ECOs through the release process and make sure they’re implemented in a controlled manner.
 Develop spaces for builds including workspace, tools, shelving for inventory and finished goods
 Manage inventory for prototype and integration builds including receiving parts, managing incoming quality control, stocking parts and prepping for builds.
 Make sure that prototype builds happen smoothly and as quickly as possible. Run daily standups or other methods of work tracking and motivation to make sure builds remain unblocked. 
 Organize and plan work. Motivate team members. Track progress and issues. Communicate with stakeholders and close out issues.
 Manage the configuration of our fleet of prototype printers. Maintain an up to date inventory of prototype printers, their configuration, status and use. Ensure that reworks and retrofits happen quickly and successfully.
 Improve processes across mechanical engineering to support the smooth development of products
 Broadly support the mechanical engineering team and mechanical engineering manager as project manager embedded in that team
 About You: 
 Demonstrates motivation to bring amazing products to life by pushing yourself, your peers and the development process forward
 Consistent and organized to make sure we’re doing everything we can to succeed
 Ready to get your hands dirty filling gaps and leading by example
 Can jump between organizing data to organizing people and back during the course of a day
 A working knowledge of technical documentation and the desire to keep learning in this area
 Build bridges between team leads and key doers on teams to quickly solve problems and blockages
 Bonus Skills: 
 Depth in mechanical engineering, electrical engineering or integration software
 Data analysis and spreadsheet wizardry
 Experience with PLM systems
 Our Perks & Benefits: 
 Unlimited 3D printing with any Formlabs material on any Formlabs printer
 An equity program that will let you build wealth through RSUs
 Healthcare coverage (medical, dental, vision) that includes a totally free employee-only plan, effective starting on your first day on the job
 401K matching with no vesting or tenure requirement
 Generous parental leave (fully paid up to 16 weeks)
 Flexible time off so you can take time when you need it
 Six-week fully paid sabbatical after hitting tenure milestones (with the option to take an additional six weeks after that)
 Free on-site parking & pre-tax commuter benefits
 Free on-site lunch, snacks, beverages, treats, beer kegs, and employee-favorite local coffee and espresso
 Self-driven professional development opportunities like conferences, trade shows, and hackathons
 One-of-a-kind activities and events like monthly socials, the annual weekend summer camp, a can’t-miss company hackathon, and lots of other social opportunities

title: Operations Program Manager
content:
About Formlabs 
 To reinvent an industry, you have to build the best team. Join Formlabs if you want to bring ground-breaking professional 3D printers to the desktop of every designer, engineer, researcher, manufacturer, and artist in the world. Formlabs manufacturing operations are the key to placing powerful digital fabrication tools into the hands of designers and engineers around the world. Manufacturing thousands of printers is already an enormous task – and the complexity will grow as we build tens and even hundreds of thousands of electronic products each year. 
 Job Summary 
 The Operations Program Manager (OPM) will play a critical role in scaling the production of Formlabs' 3D printers and ensuring smooth and efficient manufacturing operations in the Shenzhen Bay area. You will be a key leader in new product introduction (NPI), managing the entire lifecycle from concept to mass production. This role requires close collaboration with cross-functional teams in engineering, supply chain, quality, and production, both internally and with our manufacturing partners. 
 Key Responsibilities 
 Lead NPI programs for new 3D printers and accessories, ensuring successful product launches that meet quality, cost, and delivery targets. 
 Develop and execute comprehensive manufacturing plans, including capacity planning, production scheduling, and materials management. 
 Collaborate closely with engineering teams to ensure Design for Manufacturing (DFM) principles are implemented and to resolve any production challenges. 
 Manage relationships with contract manufacturers and other key suppliers in the region, ensuring adherence to quality standards and production schedules. 
 Identify and implement process improvements to optimize production efficiency, reduce costs, and enhance product quality. 
 Proactively manage risks and issues, developing mitigation plans and escalating concerns as needed. 
 Communicate program status and updates to key organizational stakeholders, including executive leadership. 
 Required Skills and Experience 
 Bachelor's degree in Engineering or a related field. MBA is considered a plus
 5+ years of experience in operations program management, preferably in the consumer electronics or high-tech manufacturing industry. 
 Results-oriented and attention to detail
 Proven track record of successfully launching new products into mass production. 
 Strong understanding of manufacturing processes, quality control systems, and supply chain management. 
 Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build relationships and influence stakeholders at all levels. 
 Familiarity with Lean manufacturing principles and Six Sigma methodologies.
 Fluency in English and Mandarin Chinese.
 Ability to travel up to 40%

title: Print Production Intern (Winter/Spring 2027)
content:
About Formlabs: 
 A 3D printer is one of the most demanding machines you can build.
 Lasers, optics, precision motion, thermals, airflow, materials handling, chemistry, sensing, controls, and software all have to work at micron-scale precision, for thousands of layers, with almost no tolerance for error. Making that work reliably is an extraordinary engineering problem.
 That’s what we do.
 At Formlabs, we’re building 3D printers that are changing the way things get made. We have the smartest minds across every engineering discipline, and the technology they’re building is deployed at more than 50,000 industry leaders worldwide, including Apple, Google, Tesla, New Balance, and NASA.
 Your Impact: 
 As a Print Production Intern on our Sales Enablement Team, you will support our showroom and print production initiatives, including printer maintenance, SLA and SLS print production, and print farm clean-up and logistics to ensure a safe and inspiring environment to produce 3D printed solutions.
 Internship Term: Winter/Spring 2027 (January 11 - April 30)
 Commitment : Full-time (40 hours/week)
 Location: Onsite in Somerville, MA (in-person)
 The Job 
 Support on design modifications, part layout and slicing for 3D print optimization.
 Support 3D print production including printing, troubleshooting and maintenance across SLA and SLS printers and all Formlabs materials. 
 Post process, sand and finish parts.
 Support the team in space maintenance to ensure top of the line health and safety in the showroom and production spaces.
 Create and identify opportunities for space improvements to optimize production, printer utilization, quality control measures, and maintenance while ensuring health and safety of the space and everyone who uses it.
 You 
 Enjoy working independently.
 Are highly organized and interested in helping streamline processes.
 Have 3D printing experience and are motivated to become a 3D printing expert.
 Are Able to lift 40-80 lbs.

content:

 Role Description
 As a Production Equipment Technician, your time will be split between rapid-response hardware troubleshooting and general factory operations. You will be responsible for diagnosing mechanical and electrical failures on 3D printers, executing preventative maintenance protocols, and performing component-level swaps to keep production moving. Additionally, you will own the organization of the warehouse and factory floor, ensuring that consumables are stocked, inventory is accurate, and the environment meets strict operational and cleanliness standards. This is a full-time, hourly role for a proactive problem-solver who enjoys working with their hands and optimizing physical spaces.
 Responsibilities
 Diagnose, troubleshoot, and repair electro-mechanical issues on 3D printers and support equipment.
 Rapidly respond to hardware faults on the production floor to minimize downtime and maintain throughput targets.
 Execute routine preventative maintenance (PM) schedules and calibration cycles.
 Manage hardware inventory, track spare parts usage, and restock production stations with critical consumables.
 Maintain a highly organized, clean, and safe factory environment using workplace organization standards.
 Document maintenance logs, repair actions, and component failures accurately.
 Collaborate with production operators and communicate equipment status clearly to operations leadership.
 Requirements
 Strong mechanical, electrical, or technical aptitude (e.g., experience repairing electronics, robotics, automotive components, appliances, or 3D printers).
 Proficiency using basic hand tools, precision measuring instruments, and navigating digital diagnostic interfaces.
 Ability to read technical documentation, assembly guides, or schematics.
 A rapid-response mindset—capable of prioritizing urgent equipment failures under tight timelines.
 Excellent spatial organization and inventory control skills.
 Prior experience in a manufacturing, technical support, hardware testing, or warehouse environment preferred.
 Work Environment and Physical Demands
 Work in a high-tech manufacturing environment with exposure to machinery noise, temperature changes, and particulate materials.
 Ability to stand, walk, and navigate the production floor for extended periods.
 Lift and move hardware or inventory weighing up to 50 pounds as needed.
 Perks & Benefits
 Comprehensive Healthcare Benefits through UMR (United Healthcare Provider Network)
 Vision and Dental included
 FSA/HSA options
 PTO accrual starting on day one—up to 3 weeks (120 hours) per year
 Commuter Benefits
 Fertility Benefits and Parental Leave

title: Senior 3D Printing R&D Engineer

 Lasers, optics, precision motion, thermals, airflow, materials handling, chemistry, sensing, controls, and software all have to work at micron-scale precision, for thousands of layers, with almost no tolerance for error. Making that work reliably is an extraordinary engineering problem.
 That’s what we do.
 At Formlabs, we’re building 3D printers that are changing the way things get made. We have the smartest minds across every engineering discipline, and the technology they’re building is deployed at more than 50,000 industry leaders worldwide, including Apple, Google, Tesla, New Balance, and NASA.
 Our growing R&D team is a mix of mechanical, systems, and software engineers. We develop and maintain the Formlabs printing process. Our team works closely with other engineering teams to research next-generation printers and materials. We use engineering, physics, and experimentation to turn ideas into beautiful and reliable products.
 If you are a systems thinker who enjoys working in a multi-disciplinary environment we would love you to join our R&D team as a Senior 3D Printing R&D Engineer.

 Create new 3D printing techniques - from developing new printer architectures to validating minute changes in Galvo control

 You: 
 2+ years post-graduate experience

 Have experience with experiment design and data analysis

 Familiar with mechanical design, mechatronics, and CAD modeling

 Previous work on a consumer product

title: Senior 3D Print Optimization Engineer
content:
A 3D printer is one of the most demanding machines you can build.
 Lasers, optics, precision motion, thermals, airflow, materials handling, chemistry, sensing, controls, and software all have to work at micron-scale precision, for thousands of layers, with almost no tolerance for error. Making that work reliably is an extraordinary engineering problem.
 That’s what we do.
 At Formlabs, we’re building 3D printers that are changing the way things get made. We have the smartest minds across every engineering discipline, and the technology they’re building is deployed at more than 50,000 industry leaders worldwide, including Apple, Google, Tesla, New Balance, and NASA.
 The Print Optimization Team takes on the challenge of optimizing the intersection of hardware, software, and materials to deliver industry leading print performance. We strive to make our SLA & SLS product line print parts as quickly, reliably, easily, accurately, and beautifully as possible. We are a collaborative team, with a diverse background, passionate about pushing the boundaries of print performance across our product lines.
 As a 3D Print Optimization Engineer, you will be continuously using your problem-solving skills to drive improved performance. 
 We are customer focused, and the first step in tackling the problem is understanding what the performance boost we are trying to achieve and how many customers will benefit. Will customers be able to print parts faster? More reliability? Will they be easier to post-process, or print more accurately? 
 If you’re excited about process optimization, solving multi-disciplinary challenges, and bringing the best print performance to market, we want you as a Senior 3D Print Optimization Engineer. 
 The Job: 
 Push the capabilities of our SLA & SLS 3D printing platforms
 Architect 3d printing optimization methodologies that result in better printer performance
 Drive root cause analysis, considering mechanics, fluid dynamics, software, chemistry, optics, electronics, thermodynamics, and customer behavior
 Design efficient experiments that tease out underlying behavior in a complicated system of variables
 Tackle multi-disciplinary problems
 Develop and commercialize solutions that make a real and immediate impact on customer print performance

It’s worth noting that this is not like the typical shop floor manufacturing engineering management role at a manufacturing plant.
 The Job :
 Lead the activities of a team of manufacturing engineering professionals responsible for supporting an extended team of global manufacturing, supply chain, quality professionals. 
 Ongoing sustainment of manufacturing lines at our contract manufacturers + transition into production and support. 
 Characterize process & product failures on our manufacturing line, root cause investigations, corrective actions, and mistake-proofing at suppliers and contract manufacturers for component/module/product new builds and refurbishments.
 Own manufacturing process (e.g. assembly, printer calibration, verification testing, etc.) control and issue prevention; implementing tools, equipment and process methods to ensure industry-leading reliability, quality, and yield.
 Drive team collaboration and support across projects/programs as a player coach on complex engineering and operational challenges. 
 Own manufacturing technical readiness as a critical member of our cross-functional NPI teams, with specific emphasis on manufacturing return of experience, producibility, cost effectiveness, industrialization; negotiate conflicting requirements, identify lessons-learned and DFM/DFA/DFSS opportunities and share/escalate to upstream design engineers and downstream sustaining engineers.
 Manage the details of transition into manufacturing or industrialization, including resolution of first article inspections (FAI) and product/fixture assembly issues; drive maturity of manufacturing readiness; secure mass production capacity, throughput, yield, and process capability.
 You :
 B.S. degree in engineering; mechanical, manufacturing engineering, aerospace, industrial, or related/equivalent field. 
 3+ years experience in an engineering management or engineering team leadership role.
 5+ years of technical skills, preferably experience in manufacturing engineering roles for complex electro-mechanical product industrialization at scale, including machined, sheet metal, injection molded, PCBA, linear motors, LCD, cables, and plastic components.
 Experience with remotely managed NPI and contract manufacturers, including transitioning high accuracy products from prototype to mass production.
 Expertise in production quality metrics, GD&T, and process/equipment qualification procedures.
 Proficient in methods for statistical analysis (e.g. DOE, comparison testing, Gage R&R), structured problem solving (e.g. A3, 8D, DMAIC), fault-tree), and process control (e.g. statistical process control, process capability Cp/Cpk).
 Willing to work onsite, in a fast paced environment, and occasionally coordinate with colleagues in different time zones during late evening local hours.
 Travel to vendors, suppliers, and production facilities (mostly in China) from time to time (~10-20%)
 Bonus : 
 Experience with Proto, EVT, DVT, PVT, and MP product development process & life cycle
 A Six Sigma Black Green/Black Belt certified professional who can still apply and teach the problem solving and statistical body of knowledge.

 On Shape of Solidworks CAD modeling skills

title: Senior Embedded Software Engineer
content:
About Formlabs 
 To reinvent an industry, you have to build the best team. Join Formlabs to build the tools that let anyone bring their ideas to life.
 Formlabs printers steer lasers with galvanometers, hold resin at temperature, read their own tilt and vibration, and know which material is loaded into them. Firmware ties all of it together. Every day, our printers print more than 10,000 parts: surgical guides, dental restorations, hearing aid shells, and prototypes. When the firmware is wrong, a 14-hour print fails, and a clinician does not get the part they were expecting on Tuesday.
 We think the engineer who writes the control loop should also be able to write the kernel driver under it, the touch screen above it, and the message it sends to the cloud. Handing each of those to a separate team kills ownership. Here, you own your product.
 What You'll Do 
 Build once, run everywhere.** Extend the Formlabs architecture with a "printer abstraction layer", so that one codebase drives several printer families. When a new machine arrives, you write its HAL. You do not copy paste code.
 Own the whole path.** Write kernel modules for sensors that have no driver. Write 1-Wire and RFID drivers for consumables. Build the Qt 6 / QML touch UI and the GStreamer camera stream. Connect the machine to the cloud and our new Formlabs mobile app over MQTT with generated protobuf interfaces.
 Ship to both ends.** Bring up prototype machines that don't have names yet, and push features to the tens of thousands of printers already in the field, often in the same week.
 You'll write mostly C++ and Python, plus some Go and TypeScript.
 You won't wait for board delivery to test your work. An MCU simulator and UI automation let you run much of the stack on your laptop, inside a dev container with the cross-compilation SDKs already installed. CI flashes nightly images onto real printers and runs real prints. Our tools here can always be better, and fixing what's still rough is also part of the job.
 About You 
 You have written code that lives on hardware products (consumer, medical, defense, or industrial) for somewhere between 2 and 100 years of your life.
 You can write filters, control loops, state machines, and RPC from scratch in C, C++, or Python.
 You would rather put a logic analyzer on the bus than argue about whose layer the bug is in.
 Slow feedback loops make you impatient, so you fix them.
 You can explain a timing bug to a mechanical engineer without talking down to them.

 Your Impact: 
 We're looking for a Senior Manager, Global Amazon Marketplace to own Formlabs' presence and growth on Amazon across nearly every marketplace we operate in — North America, Europe, Japan, Australia, and beyond.
 As the Senior Manager, Global Amazon Marketplace , you'll be the global owner of our Amazon channel and its P&L. You'll define the strategy — what we sell, where, and how — across catalog, content, advertising, pricing, and inventory, and turn Amazon into a scalable, profitable growth engine for both our professional and prosumer product lines. This is a senior, high-ownership individual-contributor role: you'll set the multi-year roadmap, make the build-vs-partner and 1P-vs-3P calls, represent the channel to marketing and commercial leadership, and manage the agency and tooling relationships needed to scale. You'll navigate the realities of selling a premium, considered-purchase hardware product on a velocity-driven marketplace, across a dozen-plus geographies, currencies, and regulatory environments.
 What You'll Do: 
 Own the global Amazon P&L across all active marketplaces (US, CA, MX, UK, DE, FR, IT, ES, NL, JP, AU, and expansion markets), including revenue, margin, and growth targets.
 Set the multi-year marketplace strategy and roadmap: which SKUs and product lines to list in which geos, when and how to enter new marketplaces, and Seller vs. Vendor Central approach per region.
 Own the full catalog and listing experience — titles, A+ / Enhanced Brand Content, Brand Store, imagery, variations, and localization — directing our creative and product marketing partners.
 Set and manage the Amazon Advertising strategy (Sponsored Products, Brands, Display, DSP) to hit efficiency and growth goals, integrated with the broader paid media plan.
 Own pricing, promotions, and deal calendars (Prime Day, seasonal events) in a way that protects brand equity and channel health across our DTC, B2B, and reseller ecosystem.
 Partner with operations and supply chain on FBA/FBM strategy, inventory forecasting, cross-border fulfillment, and account health across geos.
 Define the measurement framework for the channel and report performance, risks, and recommendations directly to marketing and commercial leadership.
 Lead cross-functional programs across ecommerce, lifecycle, creative, product, legal, and regional sales to launch new products on Amazon and keep the experience consistent with formlabs.com.
 Own global Amazon account integrity and compliance — Brand Registry, IP/counterfeit enforcement, and marketplace policy across regions.
 Build and manage the operating model for the channel — agency partners, tooling, and cross-functional workflows — scaling through influence and partnership rather than headcount.
 About You: 
 8+ years managing Amazon marketplaces at scale, including multi-geography or global responsibility, preferably for a hardware, electronics, or considered-purchase brand.
 Demonstrated ownership of a channel P&L, with a track record of driving profitable growth and making the strategic calls (1P/3P, marketplace expansion, build vs. partner).
 Deep, hands-on expertise across Seller Central and/or Vendor Central, Amazon Advertising, Brand Registry, and A+ content.
 Strong commercial and analytical instincts — you can model unit economics, size opportunities, and translate marketplace data into decisions and narratives for leadership.
 Experience operating across multiple marketplaces, currencies, and localization requirements.
 Experience influencing and aligning senior cross-functional and cross-regional stakeholders without direct authority; comfort building operating models and managing agencies and vendors.
 Exceptional written and verbal communication skills.
 Strong bias for action and comfort operating with ambiguity in a fast-moving environment.
 Strong curiosity about our customer base, product, and technology.
 Experience with ecommerce and analytics tooling (e.g., Shopify, Google Analytics, BigQuery) and Amazon-native tools (e.g., Helium 10, Jungle Scout, Pacvue, or similar) is a plus.
 Familiarity with cross-border trade, marketplace tax/compliance, and 3P/reseller dynamics is a plus.
 Why Join Us? 
 Be part of an innovative company at the forefront of the 3D printing industry.
 Collaborate with a team of passionate, driven professionals in a fast-paced environment.
 Enjoy a culture that values creativity, learning, and delivering excellence.

title: Senior Materials Scientist
content:
A 3D printer is one of the most demanding machines you can build.
 Lasers, optics, precision motion, thermals, airflow, materials handling, chemistry, sensing, controls, and software all have to work at micron-scale precision, for thousands of layers, with almost no tolerance for error. Making that work reliably is an extraordinary engineering problem.
 That’s what we do.
 At Formlabs, we’re building 3D printers that are changing the way things get made. We have the smartest minds across every engineering discipline, and the technology they’re building is deployed at more than 50,000 industry leaders worldwide, including Apple, Google, Tesla, New Balance, and NASA.
 Materials development presents one of the greatest opportunities to innovate in 3D printing, unlocking new applications in different industries such as engineering, consumer, manufacturing, automotive and healthcare. Our materials science team works closely with product management, hardware and software teams to develop new materials that push the boundaries of what can be done with 3D printing.
 If you are a scientist or engineer with experience in polymer development who’s excited to break new ground in an industry that’s moving at lightning speed, we want you as a Materials Scientist .
 The Job: 
 Conduct research and develop world-class materials for 3D printing from initial lab explorations to validation and commercialization
 Collaborate with hardware and software engineers to ensure new and existing materials print on our hardware seamlessly and reliably
 Design and perform experiments, and use the results to inform and develop materials performance improvements
 Partner with product management, hardware, and software engineers to continuously improve our materials
 You: 
 A creative and resourceful problem-solver, balancing speed and scientific rigor in a dynamic environment
 Have solid understanding of the fundamentals of materials science and polymer development
 Passionate about testing and troubleshooting, not afraid to test hundreds of times
 Love to harness data; can design and conduct rigorous experiments to optimize materials
 Can work autonomously and take initiative to learn new skills to complete an objective
 Understand the value of good documentation
 Excited to collaborate with a diverse group of scientists and engineers
 B.S., M.S., or PhD in a relevant science or engineering field (all are welcome)
 Bonus Skills: 
 Experience developing materials for 3D printing, especially for SLA/DLP or SLS printers!
 3D CAD modeling
 Programming skills (Python, Matlab, SQL, etc)
 Our Perks: 
 Robust equity program to build future wealth through RSUs
 Comprehensive healthcare coverage (Medical, Dental, Vision)
 401K matching and access to financial advisors
 Generous paid Parental Leave (up to 16 weeks)
 Tenure-based paid Sabbatical Leave (up to 6 weeks)

 And of course… unlimited 3D prints

title: Senior Mechanical Engineer
content:
A 3D printer is one of the most demanding machines you can build.
 Lasers, optics, precision motion, thermals, airflow, materials handling, chemistry, sensing, controls, and software all have to work at micron-scale precision, for thousands of layers, with almost no tolerance for error. Making that work reliably is an extraordinary engineering problem.
 That’s what we do.
 At Formlabs, we’re building 3D printers that are changing the way things get made. We have the smartest minds across every engineering discipline, and the technology they’re building is deployed at more than 50,000 industry leaders worldwide, including Apple, Google, Tesla, New Balance, and NASA.
 If you’re energized by the idea of making the impossible happen, come join us as a Senior Mechanical Engineer.
 Include a portfolio with your application to show us what you can do. 
 The Job: 
 The job is to ship the best desktop 3D printers on the market:
 Prototype new mechanisms, from precision latches to revolutionary pumps and valves to surfaces measured in microns
 Test materials that push the boundaries of what 3D printing can do
 Research 3D printing challenges and rethink every subprocess to push technology forward
 Analyze, validate, and iterate on electro-mechanical systems
 Model everything from brackets to hinges to complex parts in CAD, creating well-specified, accurate drawings
 Partner with Global Sourcing and Manufacturing Teams to bring designs from prototype to mass production 
 Flex your global savvy by working with teams around the world, virtually and in-person. Intermittent travel is expected. 
 Apply your knowledge of manufacturing techniques like injection molding and sheet metal fabrication to the world of 3D printing
 Solve customer problems by using your engineering skills to eliminate friction at every stage of their workflow
 You: 
 You can’t wait to build a precision tool that combines the power of injection molding with the beauty of the iPhone.
 You have 2+ years of industry experience 
 You want to build a precision tool that is beautiful inside and out ( but don’t take our word for it )
 You know how to partner with people in any role with the genuine goal of getting work done and doing it well
 You love the gritty details of part design, material selection, and manufacturing techniques, because you know it’s important to commit to a vision and fail fast
 You craft elegant designs that function with efficiency and simplicity
 You work confidently in 3D CAD software (Solidworks/Onshape) to design components, produce drawings, and build assemblies 
 You deeply understand the full product development cycle
 If you have Python skills, experience with contract manufacturers, know PLM or document control systems, or have a passion for industrial design, we want you to apply! 
 Our Perks & Benefits: 
 Unlimited 3D printing with any Formlabs material on any Formlabs printer
 An equity program that will let you build wealth through RSUs
 Healthcare coverage (medical, dental, vision) that includes a totally free employee-only plan, effective starting on your first day on the job
 401K matching with no vesting or tenure requirement
 Generous parental leave (fully paid up to 16 weeks)
 Flexible time off so you can take time when you need it
 Six-week fully paid sabbatical after hitting tenure milestones (with the option to take an additional six weeks after that)
 Free on-site parking & pre-tax commuter benefits
 Free on-site lunch, snacks, beverages, treats, beer kegs, and employee-favorite local coffee and espresso
 Self-driven professional development opportunities like conferences, trade shows, and hackathons
 One-of-a-kind activities and events like monthly socials, the annual weekend summer camp, a can’t-miss company hackathon, and lots of other social opportunities
 You don’t need to check every box to apply for a role. If you love working with hardware, spending time with smart people, solving hard problems, and winning, we want to hear from you.

title: Senior R&D Reliability/Test Engineer
content:
About Formlabs: 
 A 3D printer is one of the most demanding machines you can build.
 Lasers, optics, precision motion, thermals, airflow, materials handling, chemistry, sensing, controls, and software all have to work at micron-scale precision, for thousands of layers, with almost no tolerance for error. Making that work reliably is an extraordinary engineering problem.
 That’s what we do.
 At Formlabs, we’re building 3D printers that are changing the way things get made. We have the smartest minds across every engineering discipline, and the technology they’re building is deployed at more than 50,000 industry leaders worldwide, including Apple, Google, Tesla, New Balance, and NASA.
 Your Impact: 
 The Reliability Engineering Team is the company's independent voice on product robustness, ensuring our hardware products are reliable so that Customers spend more time printing and less time troubleshooting. We architect effective testing strategies, engineer advanced electro-mechanical test rigs, and extract valuable, actionable insights from the data. 
 Are you a versatile and curious engineer who can see the whole system—from the smallest part to the user's workflow? Can you take complex data and turn it into a clear, compelling story? If so, join our small and agile R&D Reliability Engineering Team. 
 What You’ll Do: 
 Develop, execute, and manage system, subsystem, and component level validation test plans to ensure products meet design and reliability requirements. 
 Perform hands-on and data-driven root cause analysis (RCA) of electromechanical subsystems and field failures, utilizing common problem-solving methodologies and a "physics of failure" approach.
 Design, build, and implement automated testing equipment for subsystem characterization and reliability/environmental testing.
 Collaborate with R&D design teams throughout product development to perform risk assessments, manage continuous testing, and contribute to design reviews, influencing product design for reliability from day one.
 Analyze field failure data to identify trends, prioritize investigations based on business value, and develop clear, actionable corrective action plans (CAPAs).
 Our team did the testing to ensure Form 4 would be the most reliable printer Formlabs has ever built: 
 LCD & Light Engine: Developed custom rigs to simulate UV light and heat, continuously monitoring performance over thousands of hours.
 Mixer Scraper: Tested our proprietary debris detection hardware to protect the LPU from damage.
 Z-Axis: Conducted millions of cycles of accelerated lifetime testing to ensure consistent motion.
 Tank Film: Developed custom pneumatic fixtures to ensure that tank tension remained high after tens of thousands of layers.
 Cartridge & Dispense System: Optimized cartridge geometry to ensure reliable dispensing of all kinds of Formlabs materials.
 Watch here to see a breakdown of these systems in action! 
 About You: 
 Well-versed with complex electromechanical systems and passionate about understanding what it takes to make them work reliably.
 Have 2+ years of experience with testing a wide range of sensors, actuators, and mechanical components.
 Have experience developing system test plans and know how to execute them efficiently within fast-paced product development timelines.
 Can prototype and run your own tests, from experimental setup to hardware and software implementation in Python.

title: SLS Materials Scientist
content:
A 3D printer is one of the most demanding machines you can build.
 Lasers, optics, precision motion, thermals, airflow, materials handling, chemistry, sensing, controls, and software all have to work at micron-scale precision, for thousands of layers, with almost no tolerance for error. Making that work reliably is an extraordinary engineering problem.
 That’s what we do.
 At Formlabs, we’re building 3D printers that are changing the way things get made. We have the smartest minds across every engineering discipline, and the technology they’re building is deployed at more than 50,000 industry leaders worldwide, including Apple, Google, Tesla, New Balance, and NASA.
 Materials development presents one of the greatest opportunities to innovate in 3D printing, unlocking new applications in different industries such as engineering, consumer, manufacturing, automotive and healthcare. Our materials science team works closely with product management, hardware and software teams to develop new materials that push the boundaries of what can be done with 3D printing.
 If you are a scientist or engineer with experience in polymer development who’s excited to break new ground in an industry that’s moving at lightning speed, we want you as an SLS Materials Scientist .
 The Job 
 Build world-class SLS materials for 3D printing from initial lab explorations to validation and commercialization
 Lead research that pushes the boundaries of SLS material performance, turning discoveries into next-gen solutions.
 Partner with product, hardware, and software teams to iterate and improve material performance based on customer feedback
 Develop methodologies to evaluate material formulations in coordination with SLS print systems —balancing material chemistry, thermal dynamics, and printing parameters
 You 
 Experience bringing a new material to market from ideation to production
 Have a solid understanding of the fundamentals of materials science and polymer product development
 Hands-on experience in thermo-plastic engineering
 Passionate about testing and troubleshooting, not afraid to test hundreds of times
 Love to harness data; can design and conduct rigorous experiments to optimize materials
 Can work autonomously and take initiative to learn new skills to complete an objective
 Understand the value of good documentation
 B.S., M.S., or PhD in a relevant science or engineering field (all are welcome)
 Bonus skills: 
 Experience developing materials for 3D printing, especially for SLA/DLP or SLS printers!

title: Social Media and Community Operations Specialist
content:
**This hybrid role has a 3-day weekly on-site expectation in our Budapest office.** 
 At Formlabs , we’re building the tools that make it possible for anyone to bring their ideas to life, from cutting-edge products to life-saving medical devices. Our 3D printing technology powers innovation at more than 50,000 industry leaders worldwide, including Apple, Google, Tesla, New Balance, and NASA. Together, we’re helping everyone design, prototype, and manufacture faster than ever before.
 We are looking for a highly motivated Social Media & Community Operations Specialist to join our team in Budapest.
 This role is designed for a data-driven technical storyteller and community architect —someone who thrives on the intersection of creative marketing and technology. You will be the bridge between Formlabs’ industry-leading innovation and our global online community, driving our affiliate program, social media operations, and scaling our presence across specialized professional forums.
 The Job: 
 Social Media & Content Operations
 Content Collaboration: Work closely with our social media and video content creators to develop editorial calendars that translate complex 3D printing workflows into high-quality, on-brand content.
 SMM System Management: Lead the day-to-day operations in our Social Media Management tool. You will be responsible for the technical setup, tagging, and organization of outgoing content.
 Operational Excellence: Manage the administrative side of social media, including link tracking (UTMs), asset organization, and ensuring all posts adhere to brand and technical standards before going live.
 Community, Forum & Influencer Advocacy
 Technical Forum Engagement: Proactively grow Formlabs’ presence on Reddit and other specialized industry forums. You will monitor discussions and contribute technical insights to establish Formlabs as a helpful, authoritative voice in the community.
 SEO & AEO Optimization: Strategically structure forum contributions to enhance SEO & AEO, ensuring Formlabs’ solutions are the top-cited results in both traditional search and AI-driven answer engines.
 Influencer Recruitment: Drive the expansion of the Formlabs influencer network by identifying, sourcing, and onboarding high-profile technical content creators.
 Affiliate Program Management
 Program Scaling: Manage and scale the Formlabs affiliate program by growing our publisher network and driving high-intent traffic via strategic affiliate link placement.
 Platform Optimization: Maximize the full potential of our automated affiliate platform. You will leverage its advanced features—such as automated workflows, performance tracking, and tiered incentives—to scale the program efficiently.
 Performance Oversight: Lead the entire affiliate journey, from initial onboarding to ongoing performance optimization. Use data-driven insights to help affiliates succeed and maximize their impact on Formlabs’ growth.
 You: 
 Professional Experience: 3+ years of experience in social media operations, community management, or affiliate marketing within a technical or engineering-driven field.
 Industry Knowledge: A sound, technical understanding of digital fabrication and a genuine passion for 3D printing technology.
 Platform Expertise: In-depth knowledge of the technical social media and forum landscape and best practices across Instagram, X, TikTok, Facebook and Reddit.
 Search Optimization: Strong understanding of SEO and AEO principles, specifically how to structure forum contributions and social content to improve discoverability in a modern search landscape.
 Community Focus: Strong understanding of community management and affiliate marketing.
 Analytical Skills: Experience analyzing social media and community data to meet strategic objectives.
 Communication: Excellent communication skills in English. Additional EMEA language skills are a plus.
 Application Quality: Please submit an English CV and a tailored, high-quality cover letter that clearly demonstrates your fit for the role.
 We Offer: 
 Hybrid work 
 Catered lunch at the office 3 days per week 
 Private health insurance with Medicover (Blue package + hospital coverage) 
 A monthly or quarterly public transportation pass for Budapest 
 Shares in the company (we're a double unicorn company!) 
 Free beverages and snacks at the office 
 All You Can Move sports pass 
 Free 3D prints 
 An inclusive, dog-friendly office with diverse and inspiring colleagues 
 Development opportunities both in-house and off-site 
 Fun team events
 We build amazing things. Come join us!

title: Software Engineer, Business Systems
content:
Join Formlabs if you want to bring ground-breaking professional 3D printers to the desktop of every designer, engineer, researcher, and artist in the world.
 As a Software Engineer on the Business Systems, you will build the software that runs the company: the integrations, automations, internal tools, and platform extensions behind how we sell, ship, bill, and account for 3D printers used worldwide. You will write production code across our core business platforms (NetSuite, Salesforce, Shopify, and our GCP-based data platform) and see your work used by colleagues across Finance, Sales, Service, Marketing, and Operations.
 This role is built for early-career engineers, including recent graduates, who learn fast and want real ownership early. Rather than joining a single tool team on day one, you will work across several parts of our Systems department, building breadth with the opportunity to go deeper into multiple areas such as Financial Systems, Digital Systems, Data Engineering or Integrations. We hire for slope over specialized tool experience: we care more about how quickly you learn and how well you ship than about which platforms you already know.
 You will join the Systems team, which enables all Formlabs teams with enterprise applications, infrastructure, data, and security to do their best work. The team supports all areas of the company, has team members globally, and reports to the CIO.
 This role is based in our Somerville, MA office and will be a hybrid role with the expectation of at least 3 days a week in office.
 The Job: 
 Build and Ship: Write, test, and deploy production code in TypeScript/Node.js and Python: system integrations, workflow automations, internal tools, and extensions to platforms like Shopify, Salesforce, and NetSuite.
 Learn the Landscape: Work on real projects across our portfolios (Financial Systems, Digital Systems, and Data Platform) to understand how data and transactions flow from a customer order through fulfillment, billing, and financial reporting.
 Connect Systems: Build and maintain APIs, webhooks, and data pipelines that move information reliably between our eCommerce, CRM, ERP, and data warehouse.

 You: 
 Early in Your Career: 0–3 years of professional software engineering experience, including internships and co-ops. Recent graduates are strongly encouraged to apply.
 Solid Fundamentals: Working proficiency in at least one of Python or TypeScript/JavaScript, with a grasp of core concepts like data structures, APIs, and debugging, plus a willingness to pick up the other.

title: Sr.Recruiter
content:
About Formlabs: 
 A 3D printer is one of the most demanding machines you can build.
 Lasers, optics, precision motion, thermals, airflow, materials handling, chemistry, sensing, controls, and software all have to work at micron-scale precision, for thousands of layers, with almost no tolerance for error. Making that work reliably is an extraordinary engineering problem.
 That’s what we do.
 At Formlabs, we’re building 3D printers that are changing the way things get made. We have the smartest minds across every engineering discipline, and the technology they’re building is deployed at more than 50,000 industry leaders worldwide, including Apple, Google, Tesla, New Balance, and NASA.

 Formlabs Shenzhen is at a pivotal stage of accelerating our China business. As the first senior recruiting partner on the ground in Shenzhen, you will directly shape the DNA of our organization in this city — building a local talent engine from the ground up and bringing top talent into our engineering, operations, sales, and support teams. Your work will not only determine how fast the Shenzhen office grows, but also how well we grow: finding individuals who both believe in Formlabs' mission to "bring ideas to life" and thrive in a fast-paced hardware tech environment. You will collaborate closely with recruiting teams in Boston, Berlin, and across APAC — translating global best practices into the China context while feeding China-market talent insights back into the global organization.
 The Job: 
 Own the end-to-end recruiting cycle for all functions in the Shenzhen office: from intake calibration, sourcing, interview coordination, and offer negotiation through to onboarding handoff — covering engineering, manufacturing operations, sales, and functional support roles. 
 Build deep partnerships with business leaders in Shenzhen and APAC, understanding business cadence and hiring bars, and proactively anticipating hiring needs rather than reacting to them. 
 Build and maintain a local Shenzhen talent pool, developing sustained candidate pipelines in key areas such as hardware engineering, 3D printing, and smart manufacturing. 
 Own every touchpoint of the candidate experience, ensuring a process that is efficient, transparent, and reflective of Formlabs' people philosophy from first contact to first day. 
 Manage recruiting data and process health: track key metrics (time-to-fill, offer acceptance rate, channel effectiveness, etc.) and use data to drive process improvement. 
 Serve as the recruiting interface for the Shenzhen team, partnering with the global People team to ensure policies, tools, and processes are both compliant and locally adapted for the China market. 
 You: 
 Required experience: 5+ years of full-cycle recruiting experience, with at least 2 years focused on technical or hardware/manufacturing roles; experience at a foreign-owned tech company or a rapidly scaling team is preferred. 
 Sourcing capability: Strong at proactive sourcing; familiar with China's local recruiting channel ecosystem (job boards, social networks, campus channels, agency partnerships); able to reach passive candidates and build genuine connections. 
 Business partner mindset: Able to hold peer-level, insightful conversations with business leaders and understand the capability profiles of technical roles — not just keyword matching. 
 Process and data fluency: Proficient with ATS systems (Greenhouse experience a plus); habitually uses data to assess recruiting efficiency and drive improvement. 
 Communication and collaboration: Bilingual working proficiency in Chinese and English (written and verbal); able to proactively sync and communicate clearly across time zones and cultures. 
 Entrepreneurial mindset: The Shenzhen office is in a growth phase — you need to be able to define problems and drive solutions proactively in an environment with limited resources and processes still being built, rather than waiting for instructions.

 An inclusive office with diverse and inspiring colleagues
 Shares in the company
 Development opportunities both in-house and off-site
 Unlimited 3D prints
 Fun team events

title: Supply Chain Engineer
content:
About Formlabs: 
 A 3D printer is one of the most demanding machines you can build.
 Lasers, optics, precision motion, thermals, airflow, materials handling, chemistry, sensing, controls, and software all have to work at micron-scale precision, for thousands of layers, with almost no tolerance for error. Making that work reliably is an extraordinary engineering problem.
 That’s what we do.
 At Formlabs, we’re building 3D printers that are changing the way things get made. We have the smartest minds across every engineering discipline, and the technology they’re building is deployed at more than 50,000 industry leaders worldwide, including Apple, Google, Tesla, New Balance, and NASA.
 Your Impact: 
 Our Manufacturing team makes 3D printing materials at scale, and Materials is one of the fastest-growing and most strategically important parts of our product portfolio. Our resins, the photopolymers that run on every Formlabs SLA printer, are formulated by our R&D team and produced in our own manufacturing facility.
 We’re looking for a technically strong Supply Chain Engineer to own the raw-material supply chain that feeds our resin factory. You’ll manage a broad base of chemical suppliers for monomers, oligomers, photoinitiators, pigments, and additives, and you’ll work hand in hand with the factory to make sure the right materials arrive on time, at the right quality, and at the right cost. Because small changes in a raw material can change how a resin prints, this role requires real technical depth: you’ll need to understand the chemistry well enough to qualify suppliers, investigate quality issues, and partner with R&D on new formulations.
 This is a role for an engineer who has worked close to production and wants ownership over the inputs that make it run.
 The Job: 
 Raw-Material Supplier Management 
 Own relationships with a broad base of chemical raw-material suppliers, running quarterly business reviews with scorecards for quality, delivery, cost, and responsiveness.
 Manage volume allocation across dual- and multi-sourced inputs to balance cost, capacity, and risk.
 Lead supplier qualification end-to-end, including technical assessments, site audits, sample evaluation with R&D and Quality, and maintenance of the Approved Supplier List.
 Investigate raw-material quality issues to root cause, working with suppliers, Quality, and the factory on lot-to-lot variability, specifications, certificates of analysis, and corrective actions.
 Factory Partnership 
 Act as the supply chain point of contact for the resin manufacturing facility, aligning raw-material supply with production plans, batch schedules, and inventory targets.
 Spend time on the factory floor to understand how incoming materials are received, stored, handled, and consumed, and use that knowledge to improve supply decisions.
 Partner with Planning and Manufacturing to set safety stock levels, manage shelf-life and storage constraints, and prevent line-down events.
 Technical Sourcing & Alternate Materials 
 Find and qualify new raw materials that enable R&D to develop new resin properties and products.
 Build alternate-source strategies for critical inputs, especially single-source chemicals.
 Manage the controlled ramp of qualified alternate materials into regular production, coordinating R&D, Manufacturing, Quality, and Supply Chain to ensure smooth transitions without changing product performance.
 Support NPI by sourcing new inputs, setting cost targets, and ensuring supply readiness ahead of launch.
 Cost & Risk 
 Build and maintain dashboards tracking current and forward-looking raw-material and resin COGS.
 Develop should-cost models grounded in chemistry and process economics to guide negotiations and cost reduction.
 Manage pricebooks and execute price change workflows.
 Maintain a live supply risk tracker covering single-source exposure, regulatory changes, supplier health, and market conditions for key chemical inputs, and lead mitigation planning.
 Continuous Improvement 
 Lead process improvement projects across the resin supply chain, from scoping through implementation.
 Turn manual, recurring work into scalable tools and processes.
 You: 
 Bachelor’s degree in Chemical Engineering, Chemistry, Materials Science, or a closely related field.
 5+ years of experience in chemical, specialty materials, polymer, coatings, adhesives, or consumer goods manufacturing, in roles such as supplier quality, process engineering, plant operations, or raw-material sourcing.
 Direct experience working with chemical raw-material suppliers, including qualification, specifications, and quality investigations.
 Hands-on experience in or alongside a manufacturing plant, and a solid understanding of how raw-material variability affects production.
 Strong analytical skills: advanced Excel/Sheets required; SQL, Python, or Tableau a plus.
 Comfortable owning recurring processes end-to-end and leading cross-functional projects with a high degree of autonomy.
 Clear communicator with supplier technical teams, factory staff, R&D, and leadership.
 Bonus Points 
 Experience with photopolymers, UV-curable chemistry, or resin formulation.
 Familiarity with chemical regulatory and compliance requirements such as REACH, TSCA, GHS, and SDS management.
 Experience with hazardous materials handling, storage, or transport.
 ERP experience (e.g., NetSuite, SAP, Oracle).
 Graduate degree in engineering or chemistry.
 Our Benefits & Perks: 
 Unlimited 3D printing with any Formlabs material on any Formlabs printer
 An equity program that will let you build wealth through RSUs
 Healthcare coverage (medical, dental, vision) that includes a totally free employee-only plan, effective starting on your first day on the job
 401K matching with no vesting or tenure requirement
 Generous parental leave (fully paid up to 16 weeks)
 Flexible time off so you can take time when you need it
 Six-week fully paid sabbatical after hitting tenure milestones (with the option to take an additional six weeks after that)
 Free on-site parking & pre-tax commuter benefits
 Free on-site lunch, snacks, beverages, treats, beer kegs, and employee-favorite local coffee and espresso
 Self-driven professional development opportunities like conferences, trade shows, and hackathons
 One-of-a-kind activities and events like monthly socials, the annual weekend summer camp, a can’t-miss company hackathon, and lots of other social opportunities
 You don’t need to check every box to apply for a role. If you love working with hardware, spending time with smart people, solving hard problems, and winning, we want to hear from you. 
 We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

 Base pay is the other part of our compensation package, and it is carefully determined based on your skills, experience, and expected impact. Equity and base pay combine to make up your total compensation package at Formlabs.
