As the scale and diversity of content continue to grow—driven by advances in AI, new creation tools, and emerging content formats—we’re investing in intelligent systems that can understand, evaluate, manage, and route content reliably at global scale.
We’re hiring Senior Staff Machine Learning Engineers to build and scale foundational ML systems that power content understanding, safety, policy enforcement, and decisioning across Spotify. Depending on your experience and interests, you may focus on areas ranging from multimodal content understanding and platform-level ML systems to safety, risk detection, policy enforcement, and compliance.
You’ll help shape the architecture and technical strategy behind how Spotify understands and makes decisions about content at global scale. This work is foundational to delivering safe, high-quality experiences for listeners and creators while enabling new ways for people to interact with content across Spotify.
What You'll Do
Define and drive machine learning strategy across content understanding, safety, policy enforcement, and platform-level decisioning
 Build and scale production ML systems for classification, moderation, ranking, risk detection, and content evaluation
 Develop automated decisioning systems that support content quality, integrity, safety, and policy compliance at scale
 Design and deploy ML systems across multiple content modalities, including text, audio, image, and video
 Build systems capable of evaluating and making decisions about content in real time and at Spotify scale
 Enable controlled and reliable access to content and metadata for downstream products and applications
 Collaborate closely with Product, Policy, Trust & Safety, and Engineering teams to translate content standards into scalable technical solutions
 Advance automation while maintaining high standards for quality, safety, fairness, explainability, and reliability
 Provide technical leadership across teams, mentoring engineers and influencing ML engineering, evaluation, and system design best practices
Who You Are
You have significant experience designing and building production-grade machine learning systems at scale
 You have deep experience with modern ML frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, JAX, or similar
 You have experience with—or a strong interest in—multimodal machine learning across areas such as text, audio, image, or video
 You have built systems where machine learning outputs inform or automate real-world decisions
 You understand how to balance automation with quality, safety, reliability, and user experience
 You’re comfortable tackling complex and ambiguous technical problems with significant product and business impact
 You think in systems, connecting models, data, infrastructure, and decisioning to platform-level outcomes and user experiences
 You care deeply about data quality, rigorous evaluation, fairness, explainability, and system reliability
 You’re an experienced technical leader who communicates clearly, mentors others, and can influence across technical and non-technical teams
Where You Will Be
This role is based in London or Stockholm
 We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

title: Staff Backend Engineer - Content Platform
content:
We design Spotify’s consumer experience—end to end, moment to moment, across every screen, platform, and partner integration. Our mission is to make listening feel effortless, personal, and joyful for billions of users around the world. That means turning complexity into clarity across hundreds of touchpoints—from our mobile and desktop apps to the smart speakers, TVs, cars, and integrations where Spotify shows up every day. If it touches a consumer, we shape it. We bring deep insight into human behavior, design, and technology to craft experiences that feel intuitive, expressive, and unmistakably Spotify.
Policy & Safety (P&S) is a domain within Content Platform in the Experience Mission, responsible for building Spotify’s content moderation and regulatory compliance infrastructure. This includes rule engines, enforcement pipelines, policy configuration systems, and compliance data platforms that ensure safety at scale.
The team operates at the intersection of backend platform engineering, machine learning systems, and regulatory compliance, partnering closely with Licensing, Trust & Safety, Legal, and Public Affairs. Sitting on the critical path for every new content type and feature, P&S enables safety-by-default experiences while supporting global regulatory requirements and evolving product innovation.
What you'll Do
Define the technical direction for policy enforcement infrastructure 
 Architect enforcement capabilities as a shared platform designed to be consumed by multiple product teams rather
 Design and evolve multi-signal orchestration systems that enable configurable, auditable policy enforcement at scale across content types and product surfaces
 Build the data foundation that makes enforcement decisions durable and reusable
 Own the hardest API and contract decisions: schema design, versioning strategy, and how enforcement interfaces evolve without breaking the teams that depend on them
 Establish integration standards for teams onboarding onto shared enforcement infrastructure, and work directly with consuming teams to execute migrations with clean cutoffs and clear end states
 Influence architecture across detection, signal processing, and enforcement workflows so that the underlying primitives stay coherent as the platform scales
 Mentor engineers and set the bar for how the team reasons about API design, data modeling, and the downstream compliance consequences of infrastructure choices
Who You Are
Deep experience designing and operating large-scale distributed systems, APIs, event-driven pipelines, rule engines, and decision systems running in production across high-throughput environments
 Proficient in backend engineering at scale, with strong command of languages like Java, Kotlin, Go, or similar; comfortable owning data models, service contracts, and storage layer decisions
 Experienced with stream processing and event-driven architectures (Kafka, Pub/Sub, or equivalent) and the tradeoffs between batch and real-time enforcement pipelines
 You have designed systems where schema and contract stability matter as much as correctness 
 Experienced with workflow orchestration and distributed coordination, whether through dedicated orchestration frameworks like Temporal or Airflow, choreography-based event systems, or hybrid approaches, and understand the tradeoffs between each in the context of long-running, stateful enforcement workflows
 Experienced with relational and non-relational storage systems and know how to model enforcement data for auditability, immutability, and efficient querying at scale
 You understand platform engineering patterns: multi-tenant APIs, configurable rule engines, policy-driven actioning systems, and the difference between building for one team and building for many
 Familiar with observability and operational excellence, distributed tracing, structured logging, alerting, and the tooling that makes enforcement systems debuggable and auditable in production
 You have worked in regulated or compliance-adjacent environments and understand how infrastructure design decisions, log retention, schema choices, data lineage, carry legal and audit consequences
 You are comfortable in polyglot environments and can navigate existing systems thoughtfully rather than defaulting to greenfield rewrites
 You think in systems end-to-end
Where You'll Be
This role is based in London or Stockholm.

title: Staff Engineer - Content Platform
content:
Content Platform is responsible for ingesting, processing, storing, and delivering every piece of content on Spotify — from music and podcasts to audiobooks. Within Content Platform, the Media domain owns the end-to-end media pipeline, from the moment content arrives through to seamless playback for listeners around the world. We're looking for a Staff Engineer to provide architectural leadership across this media platform. You’ll help shape and drive the technical direction from ingestion through transcoding, packaging, storage, delivery, and playback. This is a role for someone who thinks in systems, understands the trade-offs between codec choices and infrastructure costs, and can drive technical strategy across multiple teams at scale.
What You'll Do
Define and drive the long-term architectural direction for Spotify's media pipeline across Content Platform.
 Lead large-scale technical initiatives that span multiple squads and organizations, including projects such as media delivery, codec rollouts, and future playback capabilities.
 Partner closely with engineering managers, product managers, and senior engineers to align technical strategy with product priorities, reliability goals, and cost efficiency, acting as a key technical counterpart for media architecture.
 Guide architectural decisions across media ingestion, transcoding, packaging, storage, content delivery, and playback.
 Author and review RFCs, architecture decision records, and technical design documents that guide engineering teams and leadership.
 Mentor senior engineers across the organization, helping raise technical quality, architectural thinking, and engineering excellence.

title: Staff Machine Learning Engineer, Home Surfaces
content:
The Personalization team makes deciding what to play next easier and more enjoyable for every listener. From Blend to Discover Weekly, we’re behind some of Spotify’s most-loved features. We built them by understanding the world of music and podcasts better than anyone else. Join us and you’ll keep millions of users listening by making great recommendations to each and every one of them.
The Surfaces Podcasts team owns podcast recommendations across some of Spotify’s most visible surfaces, including Home and the Now Playing view. We build and improve the recommendation systems that help listeners discover their next favorite show or episode while helping creators reach the right audiences.
As a Staff Machine Learning Engineer, you’ll help shape the future of personalized discovery and engagement at Spotify. You’ll work at the intersection of recommendation systems, large language models, and production-scale machine learning infrastructure to build experiences for listeners at global scale. You’ll take models from research to production, help set technical direction in ambiguous problem spaces, and solve complex personalization challenges across Spotify.
What You'll Do
Own and improve the machine learning models and systems that power the Home feed, including the Shortcuts experience.
 Design, build, and ship personalized recommendations that serve millions of Spotify listeners globally.
 Build content recommendation systems for emerging agentic and AI-powered user experiences.
 Train, fine-tune, evaluate, and optimize large language models using techniques such as supervised fine-tuning (SFT), distillation, and parameter-efficient training approaches.
 Partner closely with Product Managers, Engineers, Data Scientists, and Designers to define and execute experimentation strategies.
 Drive A/B testing, monitoring, model evaluation, and continuous optimization of recommendation quality, reliability, and cost efficiency.
 Improve ML platform capabilities, data pipelines, and production systems that support personalization at Spotify scale.
 Drive technical direction in ambiguous problem spaces and contribute to the long-term architecture of our personalization systems.
 Mentor and support other Machine Learning Engineers, sharing knowledge and helping strengthen engineering practices across the team.
Who You Are
You have deep experience building and deploying machine learning systems in production environments.
 You have deep experience with recommendation systems, ranking models, personalization, or large-scale content discovery platforms.
 You are proficient in Python and have hands-on experience building machine learning systems with PyTorch.
 You have experience with large language model training, fine-tuning, evaluation, and optimization techniques, including SFT, distillation, and LoRA.
 You have worked with large-scale inference systems and understand the challenges of latency, reliability, and cost optimization.
 You care about creating high-quality user experiences through thoughtful applications of machine learning.
 You communicate effectively with technical and non-technical partners and can influence technical decisions beyond your immediate team.
 You know how to design, execute, and interpret online experiments and A/B tests to improve user outcomes.
 You have experience operating distributed machine learning workloads using technologies such as Ray, FSDP, HSDP, or similar frameworks.
 You have experience building and maintaining data pipelines and orchestration workflows using technologies such as Flyte, Airflow, BigQuery, and cloud-based storage platforms.
Where You'll Be
We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! For this role, you can be within the North Americas region as long as we have a work location.
 This team operates within the Eastern Standard time zone for collaboration.

title: Staff Product Designer - Platform Design
content:
The Platform team creates the technology that enables Spotify to learn quickly and scale easily, enabling rapid growth in our users and our business around the globe. Spanning many disciplines, we work to make the business work; creating the infrastructure, tooling, frameworks, and capabilities needed to welcome a billion customers.
Spotify runs on the tools we've built for ourselves. They help hundreds of teams ship every day to hundreds of millions of people around the world. Now, we're sharing them.
Spotify Technology brings our proven tools and services together for engineering organisations everywhere, from global enterprises to individual developers. As AI reshapes how software gets made, we're building on years of experience solving complex engineering challenges at scale.
Platform Design makes these powerful tools feel effortless. We shape the services, products and experiences used by Spotify's engineering teams and by developers around the world. We believe great design is a competitive advantage, and developer tools deserve the same care and craft as any consumer product.
As a Staff Product Designer, you'll combine product leadership with hands-on design and engineering. You'll shape the experience strategy for a key part of the Spotify Technology portfolio, establish a distinctive visual language, and turn internal tools into products customers love using. You'll work closely with product, engineering and marketing partners, reporting to the Spotify Technology Design Director.
What You'll Do
Lead complex design challenges from early exploration through to production, creating intuitive flows, interfaces, interactions and motion that make powerful developer tools easier to use.
 Shape the visual language of Spotify Technology, bringing consistency, personality and craft across product experiences and brand touchpoints.
 Transform tools built for Spotify's engineering teams into compelling commercial products that meet the needs of developers and enterprise customers.
 Bring design to life in code, building and shipping high-quality front-end experiences with close attention to performance, accessibility and detail.
 Set experience strategy across your product area, partnering with product and engineering leaders to influence priorities, guide decisions and shape the roadmap.
 Use prototypes, storytelling and experimentation to make complex ideas tangible, build alignment and help teams navigate trade-offs.
 Explore how generative AI and agentic tools can improve design and development workflows, while creating thoughtful experiences for products used by people and AI agents.
 Raise the bar for design craft across the team, championing design systems, inclusive experiences and a culture of collaboration, feedback and continuous learning.
Who You Are
You have a strong background in product design, with experience shaping complex digital products and delivering high-quality visual and interaction design.
 You're comfortable working across strategy and execution, setting a clear product direction while staying close to the details of design and delivery.
 You can build and ship user interfaces using a modern front-end technology stack, and enjoy bringing your designs into production.
 You understand how to create cohesive visual experiences across product and brand, with a thoughtful approach to interaction, motion and design systems.
 You bring an understanding of developer tools, enterprise software or platform products, including the challenges of designing for technical audiences.
 You use generative AI and agentic tools in your work, applying sound judgement about where they add value and where human expertise matters most.
 You're comfortable navigating ambiguity, using research, data and customer insights to make informed decisions and solve complex problems.
 You communicate ideas clearly, build trust across disciplines and influence product decisions through compelling design work and storytelling.
 You care about helping others grow, welcome different perspectives and contribute to an inclusive, collaborative environment where great work can happen.
Where You'll Be
This role is based in London, UK or Stockholm, Sweden
 We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

title: State and Local Government Affairs Manager
content:
We are looking for a strategic public policy professional to join Spotify’s Global Government Affairs team in New York City. The Government Affairs team helps Spotify understand the global and local policy landscape, advocates on issues important to our business and users, and works to anticipate and mitigate policy and regulatory risks.
In this role, you’ll work closely with Government Affairs colleagues and teams across Spotify to develop positions on public policy proposals and strategies to advance them. You’ll report to the Director of Government Affairs, US & Canada, with a particular focus on state and local policy.
What You'll Do
Design and execute policymaker engagement strategies that strengthen Spotify’s relationships across priority jurisdictions, with a focus on New York City, New York State, and other key states.
 Develop expertise on public policy issues with commercial and reputational importance to Spotify, including tax, artificial intelligence, content moderation, and emerging policy matters.
 Identify and assess priority state and local public policy issues affecting Spotify, and partner with your manager and US Government Affairs colleagues to develop effective advocacy strategies.
 Collaborate with teams across Spotify, including Legal, Communications, Social Impact, Product, Compliance, and Trust & Safety, to understand business priorities, develop clear policy narratives, and shape approaches to key policy issues.
 Build relationships and partnerships with external organizations, including trade associations and civil society organizations, to advance engagement and thought leadership on priority public policy issues.
 Represent Spotify with policymakers, government officials, industry peers, and other external stakeholders in support of the company’s policy priorities.
Who You Are
You have 5+ years of experience developing and implementing public policy or government affairs strategies and working with policymakers or other public policy stakeholders.
 You have experience working in government, the private sector, a trade association, or a related public policy environment.
 You have built strong relationships with policymakers and understand how to develop trusted relationships with officials in New York City, New York State, and other priority jurisdictions.
 You have experience developing public policy strategies related to the technology sector and can translate complex policy developments into clear business implications.
 You have experience engaging senior government officials, private-sector leaders, and public policy professionals.
 You can develop and execute effective advocacy strategies while balancing multiple stakeholders and priorities.
 You communicate clearly in writing and conversation and can adapt your approach for policymakers, business leaders, and cross-functional partners.
 You build collaborative relationships across functions and levels, approach problems with sound judgment and integrity, and are comfortable operating in a changing policy environment.
 You are able to travel throughout the United States as needed, including occasionally on short notice.
Where You'll Be
This is a hybrid role based in our New York City offices (average 2 to 3 days a week required)
 Working hours? We operate within the EST zone for collaboration.

title: Tax Analyst
content:
We are currently looking for a new band member to join the Spotify Tax Team. This new band member will be an Analyst, joining the Global Indirect Tax Team. This position will report into the Senior Manager for Indirect Tax in EMEA and APAC and will be based in Stockholm, Sweden.
In your role, you will focus on compliance and reporting. Spotify reports indirect taxes in more than 90 countries globally and you will be a key member of the team responsible for ensuring the completeness, timeliness and accuracy of Spotify’s global indirect tax compliance obligations. You will work in close collaboration with global tax team members in both Stockholm and New York, and work cross functionally with various accounting and finance teams.
We are a team of highly skilled and dedicated colleagues and we offer a challenging and dynamic role in an ever changing environment with the opportunity to take on much responsibility in a rapidly growing international company. Above all, your work will impact the way the world experiences audio.
What You'll Do
Prepare indirect tax returns ensuring they are filed timely and accurate.
 Calculate indirect taxes and ensure timely payments.
 Analyze data and transactions to ensure correct reporting.
 Assist with gathering and analyzing data for indirect tax audits and internal audits.
 Support in monitoring Indirect Tax rules and regulations all over the world.
 Coordinate with, and support, Finance and Accounting teams as necessary and assist in processes that involve indirect tax.
 Assist with new tax registrations where needed.
 Work with external service providers and foreign tax authorities.
 Participate in process improvement projects
 Assist in other tax compliance areas such as digital services tax.
 Other projects as required.

University degree with relevant education such as law degree, accounting, CPA, or any combination thereof.
 Approximately 2 years of relevant tax related work experience.
 Experience from indirect tax compliance work on a global scale is a big plus.
 Excellent English skills, both verbally and written. Other language skills are helpful.
 Experience with financial systems (we use NetSuite): ERPs, consolidation tools and management reporting tools.
 Strong skills in the Google suite and/or Microsoft Office including the ability to prepare robust models and the ability and desire to learn new software platforms.
 Strong attention to detail, ability to drive work and assist with process improvements.
 Self-starter, capable of working independently with strong initiative and flexibility.
 Comfortable using AI tools to improve efficiency and quality in day-to-day work, with a willingness to explore new ways of applying them. 
 Intellectually curious, detail oriented, and eager to learn and develop every day.
 Able to work in a fast paced, informal, and often ambiguous environment.

title: Administrative Business Partner
content:
A World-Changing Company
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.
The Role
Our team of Administrative Business Partners does more than just support our leaders: we're the backbone of the busiest people at Palantir. We build positive relationships with the people we support and anticipate their needs without being asked. Our passion for helping others makes us an invaluable resource at Palantir!
As an Administrative Business Partner, you will be handling a variety of professional responsibilities, including calendaring, travel, and expenses. You are very organized and thrive off of enabling the people we support to be as productive and impactful as possible. You'll demonstrate your excellent communication skills, and exercise tact and diplomacy in helping to manage relationships with internal and external senior team members at Palantir. In this role you'll also demonstrate good judgment and critical thinking by understanding competing priorities and actioning accordingly.
Administrative Business Partner (Foundry)
Provide administrative support to a portfolio of individuals/teams across the business.
 Handle sophisticated calendars in a fast-paced environment, and prioritize commitments to enhance time and productivity.
 Book travel arrangements (domestic and international).
 Track and process expense reports.
 Help plan, support, and complete office events and external gatherings.
 Work both autonomously and in collaboration with teammates, colleagues, and external contacts.
What We Value
Ability to adjust quickly, anticipate needs, and implement autonomously, with strong attention to detail.
 Ability to interact with a wide range of teams internally and externally with thoughtfulness and tact.
 High level of integrity, confidentiality, and discretion in both internal and external interactions.
What We Require
At least three years of previous administrative or personal support experience, preferably in a fast-paced environment.
 Excellent digital literacy, including proficiency with Microsoft products (Outlook, Excel, Word, PowerPoint, etc.).
 Experience with scheduling sophisticated international and domestic travel itineraries.
 Familiarity with travel booking and expense reporting software.
Palantir is particularly interested in applicants who have a current right to work in Singapore, and we encourage Singapore citizens to apply.
Life at Palantir
We want every Palantirian to achieve their best outcomes, that’s why we celebrate individuals’ strengths, skills, and interests, from your first interview to your longterm growth, rather than rely on traditional career ladders. Paying attention to the needs of our community enables us to optimize our opportunities to grow and helps ensure many pathways to success at Palantir. Promoting health and well-being across all areas of Palantirians’ lives is just one of the ways we’re investing in our community. Learn more at Life at Palantir and note that our offerings may vary by region.
In keeping consistent with Palantir’s values and culture, we believe employees are “better together” and in-person work affords the opportunity for more creative outcomes. Therefore, we encourage employees to work from our offices to foster connectivity and innovation. Many teams do offer hybrid options (WFH a day or two a week), allowing our employees to strike the right trade-off for their personal productivity. Based on business need, there are a few roles that allow for “Remote” work on an exceptional basis. If you are applying for one of these roles, you must work from the city and or country in which you are employed. If the posting is specified as Onsite, you are required to work from an office.
If you want to empower the world's most important institutions, you belong here. Palantir values excellence regardless of background. We are committed to making the application and hiring process accessible to everyone and will provide a reasonable accommodation for those living with a disability. If you need an accommodation for the application or hiring process, please reach out and let us know how we can help.
Please note that you will never be asked to submit a payment or share financial information to participate in our interview process. If you suspect that you've been contacted by a scammer, we recommend you cease all communication with the individual and consider reporting them to the relevant authorities, such as the US FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3).

title: American Tech Fellowship
content:
A World-Changing Company
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, power decisions on the battlefield, locate missing children, and more.
Applications for the January 2027 cohort are open now through December 11, 2026. 
The Program
In the 20th century, America pioneered mass production. We built the Arsenal of Democracy and won the war. Then we left this mighty Arsenal to rust. Silicon Valley, a product of Heartland work ethic, turned its back on the American worker.
It's time to reawaken the giant.
The same spirit of practical innovation that enabled America to dominate the previous century lives on in every American factory, workshop, and garage today. Some fear the proliferation of Artificial Intelligence, but we see the opportunity for a technological and industrial renaissance.
Palantir is launching the American Tech Fellowship to arm Americans with the skills to deploy cutting-edge software in the workforce. You will have an opportunity to explore and build on Palantir's Artificial Intelligence Platform (AIP) and earn a professional certification in its use. Exceptional performers will earn an opportunity to interview for a role at Palantir or partner companies, where you can use your newfound skills to contribute to the revival of American industry.
This fellowship is about more than careers. It's about restoring the promise that hard work and determination can still change your life in America. It's an investment in American excellence, and evidence of our belief that America's greatest builders are still to be discovered.
The American worker, given the right tools and opportunity, remains our competitive advantage. It's time to prove it.
The Role
In this fellowship, you'll participate in a comprehensive training program with our partner, Ontologize, to level up your technical skills on Foundry and AIP. You'll learn how to deploy Palantir's advanced software to solve tough problems in enterprise settings and have the opportunity to engage directly with Palantir engineers and leadership.
The fellowship runs for 12 weeks, beginning on January 13, 2027. You are expected to attend live virtual sessions on two weeknights each week. We will also have optional sessions once a week and office hours throughout the duration of the program. Expect to spend 10 to 15 hours per week on instruction and project work throughout the fellowship. 
This program provides valuable training to participants and is unpaid.
The window for submitting American Tech Fellowship applications is now through December 11, 2026.
What We’re Looking For
We want builders: people who are hungry to learn whatever it takes to succeed and aren't afraid to roll up their sleeves and make it happen.
You might be that kind of person if you've taught yourself, or been the local go-to, in one or more of these areas:
 Software, data, or automation
 General-purpose programming languages such as Python, C/C++, C# / .NET, Rust, Go, Java, TypeScript/JavaScript
 Data science applications such as SQL, MATLAB, Simulink, R, Julia, Excel + VBA
 Process improvements like instrumenting, automating, or optimizing how things run
 Prototyping—i.e., testing ideas iteratively instead of waiting for perfect specs
What We Value
Show us where you've flexed that builder's mindset. That could look like:
 Formal study in computer science, electrical/mechanical/control systems engineering, physics, applied math, data science, mechatronics, robotics, or a related field
 Experience solving real problems in settings such as a factory floor, a warehouse or logistics hub, a hospital or clinic, a construction site, field service, energy or utility operations, the military, a small business, or a garage shop, especially if you automated, instrumented, or optimized a process
 Startup, maker-space, or hackathon projects that blended hardware and software, such as retrofitting equipment, building a sensor network, or deploying an edge AI model
 Publications, patents, or open-source contributions in software, data, automation, or related technical fields
If you've got the fire to learn and you've built something that moved the needle, you're the kind of American worker we designed this fellowship for.
Backgrounds in skilled trades, manufacturing, and field work, as well as in clinical or business settings, are welcome.
What We Require
2+ years of hands-on work experience in a technical setting or engaging in on-the-job technical processes
 Backgrounds in computer science, data science, physics, and engineering domains are preferred, though no formal degree is required.

title: Backend Software Engineer - Application Development
content:
A World-Changing Company
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.
The Role
Backend Software Engineers at Palantir build software at scale to transform how organisations use data. Our Software Engineers are involved throughout the product lifecycle, from idea generation, design, prototyping, and production delivery. You will collaborate closely with technical and non-technical teammates to understand our customers' problems and build products that solve them. We encourage movement across teams to share context, skills, and experience, so you'll learn about many different technologies and aspects of each product. Engineers work autonomously and make decisions independently, within a community that will support and challenge you as you grow and develop, becoming a strong technical contributor and engineering leader.
Your day-to-day workflow will vary, adapting to the requirements of our users and the technical challenges that arise. One day, you may find yourself collaborating with other engineers to architect a new system that enables a novel workflow, the next you could be fine-tuning performance to enable low-latency operational outcomes.
Our Product Development organisation is made up of small teams of Software Engineers. Each team focuses on a specific aspect of a product and work collaboratively to build cross functional capabilities, streamline user workflows and continuously improve our software's efficiency and reliability.
We’re hiring engineers who are passionate about solving real-world problems and empowering both developers and end-users to work optimally. If you’re motivated to develop reliable, performant, and scalable systems, and to design robust APIs and primitives, this role offers the opportunity to make a significant impact on our products and the people who use them.
Frontline
Foundry Software Engineers may be offered the opportunity to Frontline, an exclusive program unlike any other. This unique, short-term assignment involves being embedded with customers, allowing you to work directly with users and gain firsthand insight into how our products are used and the challenges our customers face. Unlike traditional engineering roles, Frontline immerses you in complex, ambiguous problems, empowering you to deliver impactful solutions across some of the world’s most important industries and institutions.
Some of our most successful products were built on the factory floor, addressing real-world problems for the world's most important institutions. These products were developed by some of our most successful product engineers, who began their careers in roles aligned with Frontline responsibilities, gaining a deep understanding of both our technology and our customers.
Frontliners operate across a broad spectrum of responsibilities, much like a startup CTO. They work in small teams to own the end-to-end execution of high-stakes projects. This spectrum ranges from discussing architecture and building custom web apps to conducting workshops with users and strategizing with customer executives.  Designing efficient data structures and algorithms to manage large-scale and high throughput data

 Actively improve user workflows by collaborating with cross-functional teams, ensuring seamless experiences across product boundaries and a cohesive user experience

Different backend languages, including Java, Rust, Python and Go
 Distributed systems technologies such as Kafka, Cassandra, Elasticsearch and Spark
 Docker and Kubernetes for containerisation and orchestration
 Industry-standard build tooling, including Gradle and GitHub
What We Value
A deep understanding of server-side logic, efficient data handling, and distributed systems
 Strong focus on creating user-oriented workflows and solutions, crossing product boundaries to deliver cohesive and solid user workflows that ensure a seamless and intuitive user experience
 Experience building high-quality software in a fast-paced CI/CD development environment
 Ability to work collaboratively in teams of technical and non-technical individuals and understand how technical decisions impact the people who will use what you're building
 Skill and comfort working in a constantly evolving environment with dynamic objectives and iteration with users
 Active UK Security clearance, or eligibility and willingness to obtain a UK Security clearance is beneficial but not necessary
What We Require
Experience in designing and developing features and improvements, as well as supporting and maintaining, live backend systems
 In-depth understanding of data structures, system architecture, API development for microservices frameworks, distributed systems and other backend-related concepts and best practices
 Engineering background in Computer Science, Mathematics, Software Engineering, Physics or similar field
 Strong coding skills with demonstrated proficiency in programming languages, such as Java, C++, Python, Rust, or similar languages
 Strong written and verbal communication skills and ability to iterate quickly with teammates, incorporating feedback and holding a high bar for quality

We want every Palantirian to achieve their best outcomes, that’s why we celebrate individuals’ strengths, skills, and interests, from your first interview to your longterm growth, rather than rely on traditional career ladders. Promoting health and well-being across all areas of Palantirians’ lives is just one of the ways we’re investing in our community. Learn more at Life at Palantir and note that our offerings may vary by region.
In keeping consistent with Palantir’s values and culture, we believe employees are “better together” and in-person work affords the opportunity for more creative outcomes. Therefore, we encourage employees to work from our offices to foster connectivity and innovation. Many teams do offer hybrid options (WFH a day or two a week), allowing our employees to strike the right trade-off for their personal productivity. Based on business need, there are a few roles that allow for “Remote” work on an exceptional basis. If you are applying for one of these roles, you must work from the city and or country in which you are employed. If the posting is specified as Onsite, you are required to work from an office.

title: Backend Software Engineer - Data Connectors
content:
A World-Changing Company
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.
The Role
The Connectivity team builds the software that connects Palantir’s platform to customer systems. Our connectors integrate databases, enterprise applications, cloud storage, web services, and streaming systems, enabling customers to bring data into Foundry and write back to their operational systems. From large datasets to real-time events and user-driven interactions, these connections underpin the applications and AI workflows customers build with Foundry and AIP.
You’ll build and maintain Foundry’s first-class connector suite and the shared infrastructure behind it. You’ll work across the stack, taking ownership of connector implementations, developer SDKs, and the systems that build, test, distribute, and run our connectivity software.
A central part of this work is evolving and scaling a large, established codebase. You’ll move integrations from bespoke infrastructure onto shared platform capabilities, design SDKs that enable other teams and customers to build integrations independently, and safely retire older implementations. You’ll also build observability and diagnostic tools that help users understand, monitor, and troubleshoot their connections. You’ll own improvements from design through production and use what you learn from operating connectors to strengthen the platform they share.
Technologies We Use
Java and Python for connectors, backend services, and developer SDKs
 Open-source technologies like Kafka, Kubernetes, Flink, Debezium, Iceberg
 Industry-standard build tooling, including Gradle and GitHub
 Shared job orchestration, streaming, serverless execution, and compute deployment platforms
Core Responsibilities
Build and maintain Foundry’s first-class connectors, improving performance and extending support for imports, exports, change data capture, interactive queries, and writeback as external systems and customer needs evolve.
 Improve the infrastructure that builds, tests, packages, and distributes connectors and shared libraries, including tooling across our connector monorepo.
 Design and maintain connectivity SDKs for internal teams and end users, with clear APIs, documentation, testing utilities, and development workflows that make integrations easy to author and maintain.
 Collaborate with product teams to integrate connector execution with job orchestration, streaming, and serverless platforms.
 Lead incremental migrations onto shared infrastructure, manage compatibility, and retire older implementations while preserving the workflows customers depend on.
 Develop reusable security frameworks and tooling that make secure connectivity a consistent part of connector development and execution.
 Debug production issues and performance problems across the stack, turning recurring support problems into durable fixes, automated tests, and better observability.
 Establish shared testing frameworks, compatibility checks, and release practices that keep a large connector portfolio reliable and maintainable.
 Help prepare and maintain Palantir connectivity software for open-source use, including its APIs, packaging, documentation, and contributor experience.
What We Value
An ownership mindset and a high bar for correctness, security, and automated testing, including responsibility for how software behaves in production.
 Pride in building and maintaining integrations over time, including the detailed work required to keep them reliable as upstream systems change.
 Engineering judgment that balances delivering new capabilities with simplifying existing systems and reducing operational burden.
 Empathy for developers and end users, reflected in usable SDKs, clear configuration, actionable errors, and useful diagnostics.
 Curiosity about unfamiliar systems and persistence in debugging problems across languages, APIs, services, networks, and execution environments.
What We Require
4+ years of professional software engineering experience developing external system connectors, with depth in areas such as developing batch and streaming data ingestion systems, third-party integration development, or monorepo and asset distribution frameworks. Operating on top of these technologies alone does not qualify.
 Deep expertise in Gradle, including developing custom plugins, managing multi-project builds, and optimizing build performance.
 Demonstrated ability to diagnose complex reliability and performance problems and improve systems through measured, incremental changes.
 Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work effectively across teams, incorporate feedback, and hold a high bar for quality.
Salary

title: Backend Software Engineer - Infrastructure
content:
A World-Changing Company
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.
The Role
Software Engineers at Palantir build software at scale to transform how organizations use data. Our Software Engineers are involved throughout the product lifecycle, from idea generation, design, prototyping, and production delivery. You will collaborate closely with technical and non-technical teammates to understand our customers' problems and build products that solve them. We encourage movement across teams to share context, skills, and experience, so you'll learn about many different technologies and aspects of each product. Engineers work autonomously and make decisions independently, within a community that will support and challenge you as you grow and develop, becoming a strong technical contributor and engineering leader.
Our Product Development organization is made up of small teams of Software Engineers. Each team focuses on a specific aspect of a product. Our infrastructure teams are responsible for the lowest layers of our software stack, often focused on database technologies, distributed systems, large scale data systems, security, and application infrastructure. As a Software Engineer on infrastructure working on our Foundry platform, you'll contribute high-quality code to underpin Palantir Foundry and Gotham with performant, secure, and scalable building blocks, enabling products deployed to the most important institutions in the public and private sector. You'll build the foundational capabilities that power our products used by research scientists, aerospace engineers, intelligence analysts, and economic forecasters, in countries around the world.
We’re hiring engineers who are passionate about solving real-world problems and empowering both developers and end-users to work optimally. If you’re motivated to develop reliable, performant, and scalable systems, and to design robust APIs and primitives, this role offers the opportunity to make a significant impact on our products and the people who use them.
Frontline
Foundry Software Engineers may be offered the opportunity to Frontline, an exclusive program unlike any other. This unique, short-term assignment involves being embedded with customers, allowing you to work directly with users and gain firsthand insight into how our products are used and the challenges our customers face. Unlike traditional engineering roles, Frontline immerses you in complex, ambiguous problems, empowering you to deliver impactful solutions across some of the world’s most important industries and institutions.
Some of our most successful products were built on the factory floor, addressing real-world problems for the world's most important institutions. These products were developed by some of our most successful product engineers, who began their careers in roles aligned with Frontline responsibilities, gaining a deep understanding of both our technology and our customers.
Frontliners operate across a broad spectrum of responsibilities, much like a startup CTO. They work in small teams to own the end-to-end execution of high-stakes projects. This spectrum ranges from discussing architecture and building custom web apps to conducting workshops with users and strategizing with customer executives. No two days are alike, as each day is diverse and impactful. By witnessing how customers engage with Foundry and experiencing these pain points firsthand, you’ll gain unique insights that feed directly back into our development process, helping to refine and enhance our products.
Core Responsibilities 
Building a performant search and indexing ecosystem for complex granularly permissioned data
 Contributing to open-source data processing libraries, integrating the latest innovations to achieve performance gains
 Building the distributed systems that power large scale compute workloads, orchestrating and efficiently scheduling hundreds of thousands of containers every hour
 Designing architecture and opinionated APIs to keep application developers on the happy path
 Tracing and performance observability in high scale distributed microservice architectures
 Building reliant, performant, and scalable systems for storage, auth, or asset serving to enable other product teams to build robust applications without deep domain expertise in the underlying systems
 Automating the deployment, management, and operations of complex distributed systems like Cassandra, Elasticsearch, Kafka, and more across different environments
Technologies We Use 
Different backend languages, including Java, Rust, and Go
 Open-source technologies like Cassandra, ElasticSearch, Spark, Kafka, Kubernetes, Flink
 Industry-standard build tooling, including Gradle and GitHub
What We Value
Demonstrated ability to collaborate and empathize with a variety of individuals. Able to iterate with users and non-technical stakeholders and understand how technical decisions impact them.
 Ability to learn new technology and concepts, even without in-depth experience. Experience developing and managing highly-available distributed systems is beneficial, but not required.
 Bias towards quality and thoughtful about edge cases (“anything that can go wrong will go wrong”); writes code that is defensive against all possibilities.
 Builds solutions and APIs with users in mind while maintaining a high engineering bar. Seeks to centralize and abstract complexity away from our users in order to expose simple, powerful APIs for consumers.
 Active US Security clearance, or eligibility and willingness to obtain a US Security clearance is beneficial, but not necessary.
What We Require
Engineering background in Computer Science, Mathematics, Software Engineering, Physics or similar field.
 Strong coding skills with demonstrated proficiency in programming languages, such as Java, C++, Python, Rust, or similar languages.
 Familiarity with storage and data processing systems, cloud infrastructure, and other technical tools.
 Strong written and verbal communication skills and ability to iterate quickly with teammates, incorporating feedback and holding a high bar for quality.
Salary
The estimated salary range for this position is estimated to be $135,000 - $200,000/year. Total compensation for this position may also include Restricted Stock units, sign-on bonus and other potential future incentives. Further note that total compensation for this position will be determined by each individual’s relevant qualifications, work experience, skills, and other factors. This estimate excludes the value of any potential sign-on bonus; the value of any benefits offered; and the potential future value of any long-term incentives.

title: Backend Software Engineer - Infrastructure, Foundations
content:
A World-Changing Company
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.
The Role
Backend Software Engineers at Palantir build software at scale to transform how organizations use data. Our Software Engineers are involved throughout the product lifecycle, from idea generation, design, prototyping, and production delivery. You will collaborate closely with technical and non-technical teammates to understand our customers' problems and build products that solve them. We encourage movement across teams to share context, skills, and experience, so you'll learn about many different technologies and aspects of each product. Engineers work autonomously and make decisions independently, within a community that will support and challenge you as you grow and develop, becoming a strong technical contributor and engineering leader.
Our Product Development organization is made up of small teams of Software Engineers. Each team focuses on a specific aspect of a product. Our infrastructure teams are responsible for the lowest layers of our software stack, often focused on database technologies, distributed systems, large scale data systems, security, and application infrastructure. As a Software Engineer on infrastructure, you'll contribute high-quality code to underpin Palantir Foundry and Gotham with performant, secure, and scalable building blocks, enabling products deployed to the most important institutions in the public and private sector. You'll build the foundational capabilities that power our products used by research scientists, aerospace engineers, intelligence analysts, and economic forecasters, in countries around the world.
We’re hiring engineers who are passionate about solving real-world problems and empowering both developers and end-users to work optimally. If you’re motivated to develop reliable, performant, and scalable systems, and to design robust APIs and primitives, this role offers the opportunity to make a significant impact on our products and the people who use them.
Core Responsibilities 
Building a performant search and indexing ecosystem for complex granularly permissioned data
 Contributing to open-source data processing libraries, integrating the latest innovations to achieve performance gains
 Building the distributed systems that power large scale compute workloads, orchestrating and efficiently scheduling hundreds of thousands of containers every hour
 Designing architecture and opinionated APIs to keep application developers on the happy path
 Tracing and performance observability in high scale distributed microservice architectures
 Building reliant, performant, and scalable systems for storage, auth, or asset serving to enable other product teams to build robust applications without deep domain expertise in the underlying systems
 Automating the deployment, management, and operations of complex distributed systems like Cassandra, Elasticsearch, Kafka, and more across different environments
Technologies We Use 
Different backend languages, including Java, Rust, and Go
 Open-source technologies like Cassandra, ElasticSearch, Spark, Kafka, Kubernetes, Flink
 Industry-standard build tooling, including Gradle and GitHub
What We Value
Demonstrated ability to collaborate and empathize with a variety of individuals. Able to iterate with users and non-technical stakeholders and understand how technical decisions impact them.
 Ability to learn new technology and concepts, even without in-depth experience. Experience developing and managing highly-available distributed systems is beneficial, but not required.
 Bias towards quality and thoughtful about edge cases (“anything that can go wrong will go wrong”); writes code that is defensive against all possibilities.
 Builds solutions and APIs with users in mind while maintaining a high engineering bar. Seeks to centralize and abstract complexity away from our users in order to expose simple, powerful APIs for consumers.
 Active US Security clearance, or eligibility and willingness to obtain a US Security clearance is beneficial, but not necessary.
What We Require
Engineering background in Computer Science, Mathematics, Software Engineering, Physics or similar field.
 Strong coding skills with demonstrated proficiency in programming languages, such as Java, C++, Python, Rust, or similar languages.
 Familiarity with storage and data processing systems, cloud infrastructure, and other technical tools.
 Strong written and verbal communication skills and ability to iterate quickly with teammates, incorporating feedback and holding a high bar for quality.
Salary
The estimated salary range for this position is estimated to be $135,000 - $200,000/year. Total compensation for this position may also include Restricted Stock units, sign-on bonus and other potential future incentives. Collaborate with attorneys to structure, draft, negotiate, and close large commercial customer contracts and complex commercial transactions

 Advise internal partners on contract-related questions, tasks and best practices, using discretion and priority setting skills to escalate as necessary
What We Value
Ability to maintain accurate records, report project metrics and track contractual terms, using meticulous attention to detail and organization

content:
A World-Changing Company
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.
The Role
As a member of Palantir's Security Compliance team, you will develop a deep understanding of Palantir's control environment, infrastructure, and products. You will work with information security, business and product development experts, and external parties to navigate and manage commercial and international compliance frameworks (SOC/ISO 27001/17/18, ISO 9001) and geographically strategic compliance frameworks (ENS, TISAX, ISMAP, IRAP) in order to provide practical guidance on technical documentation, operational concerns, and sustainable processes that will allow us to continue to grow quickly & efficiently while also maintaining our current compliance obligations. You will additionally be a co-owner of our holistic internal risk management and internal control structures.
We are looking for a team-focused and mission-oriented compliance professional that can navigate ambiguity and uncertainty, with the ability and desire to achieve goals and drive progress in an environment where outcomes must be achieved through their own resourcefulness and initiative.
 Core Responsibilities
Assist in the performance of internal and external security assessments of Palantir products, infrastructure, and processes.
 Have a interest and general aptitude emerging technologies : from leveraging AI tooling, harnessing the capabilities of evidence automation and documentation management, and a general aptitude for agentic integration within workflows.
 Develop and maintain an understanding of Palantir’s control environment and articulate this understanding to various audiences, including internal and external stakeholders and auditors.
 Technical writing skills to enable the maturation of internal documentation and externally facing reporting of Palantir’s security posture across an array of control domains.
 Partner with thought leaders across the organization to identify and consult on key controls for risk mitigation and externally focused requirements.
 What We Value
Self-reliance, proactivity, organization, mission-oriented ambition. We will teach everything that is teachable but you will need to bring the right intangibles and attributes.
 Inherent comfort and embracement of continuous change and new challenges.
 Familiarity with basic architecture concepts of distributed cloud infrastructure
 Demonstrated communication skills to translate engineering language into compliance language and vice versa.
 Demonstrated ability to autonomously project manage and keep oneself on track with long-tail objectives.
 What We Require
2+ years of experience protecting or auditing modern and technologically complex SaaS environments.
 Experience facilitating or being the subject a major compliance framework (SOC 2, ISO 27001, etc.)
 Experience with parsing key controls in structurally complex technical and business processes.

The Role
As a member of Palantir's Security Compliance team, you will develop a deep understanding of Palantir's control environment, infrastructure, and products. You will work with information security, business and product development experts, and external parties to navigate and manage commercial and international compliance frameworks (SOC/ISO 27001/17/18, ISO 9001) and geographically strategic compliance frameworks (ENS, TISAX, ISMAP, IRAP) in order to provide practical guidance on technical documentation, operational concerns, and sustainable processes that will allow us to continue to grow quickly & efficiently while also maintaining our current compliance obligations. You will additionally be a co-owner of our holistic internal risk management and internal control structures.
We are looking for a team-focused and mission-oriented compliance professional that can navigate ambiguity and uncertainty, with the ability and desire to achieve goals and drive progress in an environment where outcomes must be achieved through their own resourcefulness and initiative.
 Core Responsibilities
Assist in the performance of internal and external security assessments of Palantir products, infrastructure, and processes.
 Have a interest and general aptitude emerging technologies : from leveraging AI tooling, harnessing the capabilities of evidence automation and documentation management, and a general aptitude for agentic integration within workflows.
 Develop and maintain an understanding of Palantir’s control environment and articulate this understanding to various audiences, including internal and external stakeholders and auditors.
 Technical writing skills to enable the maturation of internal documentation and externally facing reporting of Palantir’s security posture across an array of control domains.
 Partner with thought leaders across the organization to identify and consult on key controls for risk mitigation and externally focused requirements.
 What We Value
Self-reliance, proactivity, organization, mission-oriented ambition. We will teach everything that is teachable but you will need to bring the right intangibles and attributes.
 Inherent comfort and embracement of continuous change and new challenges.
 Familiarity with basic architecture concepts of distributed cloud infrastructure
 Demonstrated communication skills to translate engineering language into compliance language and vice versa.
 Demonstrated ability to autonomously project manage and keep oneself on track with long-tail objectives.
 What We Require
2+ years of experience protecting or auditing modern and technologically complex SaaS environments.
 Experience facilitating or being the subject a major compliance framework (SOC 2, ISO 27001, etc.)
 Experience with parsing key controls in structurally complex technical and business processes.

title: Corporate Counsel
content:
A World-Changing Company
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.
The Role
Palantir’s in‑house legal team works to proactively address legal issues so that Palantir can continue to drive positive impact in the world. As Corporate Counsel, you will serve as a key advisor on corporate governance and securities matters, leveraging your public company experience to ensure our compliance and support our growth as a public company. You will take ownership of critical areas such as investment management, trading compliance, strategic transactions, corporate governance, and public company reporting. In addition, you’ll play a central role in structuring, implementing, and administering equity compensation plans for employees globally, collaborating with cross-functional teams to align our equity programs with Palantir’s mission and values. This is a high-impact role where you will consistently work cross-functionally and with leadership teams (including the Chief Financial Officer, Chief Accounting Officer, and Chief Revenue Officer and Chief Legal Officer), and will translate complex legal requirements into clear communications and actionable strategies that support Palantir’s continued innovation and success as a public company.
In this role, you will join a team that values broad-based experience and a relentless drive to learn quickly in a dynamic environment. We prioritize practical solutions and outcomes that ensure compliance with public company requirements while maximizing benefits for our employee base and advancing Palantir’s mission. Your ability to adapt, think creatively, and work collaboratively will be essential as you take on complex issues and transactions.
What You'll Do
Advise on a range of complex equity and corporate/securities issues.
 Help manage public company filings and related internal processes.
 Work on Board, Committee, and other corporate governance matters for Palantir and our subsidiaries and joint ventures.
 Assist with a variety of corporate and securities transactions, including M&A and other strategic investments.
 Assist in management and administration of Palantir’s equity portfolio.
What We Value
Resourcefulness and the ability to solve problems, including non-traditional or undefined problems, creatively and analytically.
 Ability to work independently and collaborate with cross-functional teams.
 Ability to communicate complex legal concepts in a way that is understandable and actionable.
 Ability to prioritize and communicate deadlines with internal and external stakeholders, and build constructive, high-trust relationships across teams and functions.
 Sound judgment and composure in high-pressure situations; display discretion and integrity in all interactions.
What We Require
JD and active bar membership (or equivalent international qualification).
 4+ years’ experience as a corporate or securities attorney at a top firm or in-house (a combination is even better!)
 Knowledge of and experience with public company reporting requirements, corporate governance and board matters, and securities and strategic transactions.
 Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with an ability to distill complexity into clarity.
Salary
The estimated salary range for this position is estimated to be $135,000 - $200,000/year. Total compensation for this position may also include Restricted Stock units, sign-on bonus and other potential future incentives. In addition, you’ll play a central role in structuring, implementing, and administering equity compensation plans for employees globally, collaborating with cross-functional teams to align our equity programs with Palantir’s mission and values. Advise on a range of complex equity and corporate/securities issues.
 Help manage public company filings and related internal processes.
 Work on Board, Committee, and other corporate governance matters for Palantir and our subsidiaries and joint ventures.

 Assist in management and administration of Palantir’s equity portfolio.

Resourcefulness and the ability to solve problems, including non-traditional or undefined problems, creatively and analytically.
 Ability to work independently and collaborate with cross-functional teams.
 Ability to communicate complex legal concepts in a way that is understandable and actionable.

title: Data Engineer - Talent Acquisition Operations
content:
A World-Changing Company
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.
The Role
As a Data Engineer, you will help to build and maintain the data foundations, reporting workflows, and automations that support Recruiting and Hiring Operations. This role will work cross-functionally with Hiring Operations, Recruiters, Data, Security, Privacy, and other technical and non technical partners to turn complex recruiting processes into reliable datasets, dashboards, and operational tools. The ideal candidate enjoys working at the intersection of data engineering and business operations. You will be expected to understand how recruiting workflows generate data and build practical solutions that improve day to day operations.
This role is well suited for someone who can move fluidly between building a pipeline, debugging an integration, creating a dashboard, documenting an operating procedure, and helping stakeholders understand how to use the resulting tool.
Core Responsibilities
Build, maintain, and improve datasets and pipelines supporting Recruiting
 Integrate data from systems such as Lever, Workday, Foundry, and other recruiting systems
 Develop reporting datasets and dashboards for recruiting performance, candidate pipelines, recruiting programs, and operational audits
 Evaluate existing data integrations for opportunities to reduce latency and implement necessary changes
 Partner with central Data and platform teams on warehouse connections, schema changes, API behavior, and source-system migrations
 Support integrations between recruiting systems and internal tools including writeback of data updates
 Design data access and reporting solutions that respect confidentiality, role-based permissions, and regional or organizational access boundaries
 Create clear documentation for sensitive workflows and ensure that operational users understand the limitations of the data
 Proactively identify opportunities to improve reporting and workflows as recruiting processes change
 Partner with team members, engineering, product and business leaders to understand current user behavior and patterns across our platform
 Monitor pipelines for stability, suggest and implement efficiency initiatives
What We Value
Proven ability to build and maintain data pipelines, datasets, and analytics data products
 Hands-on experience with Foundry, Contour, or comparable data and analytics platforms
 Background working with Recruiting, HR, People, CRM, ATS, or other operational data; Lever experience preferred
 Proficiency integrating APIs, data warehouses, and SaaS systems
 Familiarity with workflow automation, writeback processes, and event-driven integrations
 Working knowledge of data governance, privacy, retention, access controls, and compliance-related workflows
What We Require
Degree in Data Science, Finance, Math, Engineering, Computer Science, Economics, Business or other quantitative fields
 1+ years of experience in a data analytical role
 Expertise in Python and data manipulation to answer complex questions. Experience with pySpark, pandas, or polars is a plus.
 Strong SQL skills and experience working with relational or structured data.
 Proficiency with BI tools, SQL, and the organization and analysis of data
 Fluency in TypeScript, or another general-purpose programming language
 Ability to create reusable data models, testing frameworks, and data quality checks
Salary
The salary range for this position is estimated to be $100,000 - $145,000/year. Total compensation for this position may also include Restricted Stock units, sign-on bonus and other potential future incentives. title: Deal Team - Business Affairs
content:
A World-Changing Company
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.
The Role
Our Deal Team members collaborate with multiple Palantir teams to proactively engage with existing and prospective commercial customers, leading the structuring and negotiation of deal terms so that Palantir can continue to drive positive impact in the world. 
As a member of the Deal Team, you will partner closely with Palantir’s Legal, Finance, Sales, and Engineering teams to drive deal execution and support our growth efforts at scale, while directly owning the development and negotiation of commercial terms for commercial customers. You will use your expertise to unite our customer’s needs and considerations with our company’s strategy, using your creativity to identify the right commercial structure and approach for each customer. You will also utilize your understanding of the business landscape and build relationships with internal partners, increasing the visibility of deal progress and forecasting impact across all levels of our organization, from analysts to C-suite executives. 
In this role, you will also support various special projects that arise at our fast-paced, mission-focused company. We’re a team that values both creativity and teamwork. Whether operating solo or collaboratively, we endeavor to achieve great results on challenging, time-sensitive deal discussions and projects. 
You'll be given open ended objectives and expected to find ways to turn them into outcomes. By focusing on the broad vision without losing sight of the details, you'll bring large and multi-phase deals to successful completion while prioritizing team outcomes over individual wins. You are able to deliver complex commercial contract and deal information in an understandable way, and can manage high touch stakeholders in a constantly shifting landscape. You are ready to become an expert on the intricate details of deal negotiations and contracts that enable Palantir to implement its cutting-edge technology to solve real-world problems. 
Core Responsibilities
Collaborate with Sales counterparts to develop the pricing terms and commercial structure for each commercial customer.
 Lead negotiations of commercial terms during the contracting process, guiding communications as appropriate for the situation.
 Draft materials in support of deal negotiations, including pricing proposals, term sheets and order forms, while advising the business on commercial structure implications including revenue impact and timing.
 Cooperate with internal Legal, Finance, Sales and Engineering teams to drive deals to execution, providing trusted guidance for navigating negotiations and procurement processes and maintaining engagement throughout the customer lifecycle to develop and negotiate commercial terms for renewal and up-sell opportunities.
 Ensure alignment of individual deal terms with company-wide strategy, while also addressing individual customer needs and considerations.
 Partner with Finance team to provide leadership with visibility of deal progress and forecasting impact.
 Present the results of our work and proposals for new deals to audiences ranging from analysts to C-suite executives, and distill your experiences with individual customers into suggested improvements for deal structures and contract terms.
What We Value
Experience drafting materials in deal negotiations such as pricing proposals, order forms, and contracts.
 Demonstrated experience approaching problems creatively and analytically.
 Ability to build strong relationships and collaborate both with a cross-functional team and with customers, leveraging effective communication as well as strong writing and customer service skills .
 Strong program/project management skills, including the ability to handle multiple competing priorities in a fast-paced environment, and meet deadlines with minimal supervision or administrative support.
 Adaptive, empathetic, and introspective; willing to learn, teach, lead and follow.
 Willingness and ability to work outside of standard business hours as needed.
What We Require 
5+ years of commercial contracting, drafting or partnership negotiation experience; experience negotiating SaaS or other technology agreements is a definite plus.
 Education: Master of Business Administration (MBA) or Juris Doctor (JD) degree, with preference of JD.
Salary
The estimated salary range for this position is estimated to be $135,000 - $200,000/year. Total compensation for this position may also include Restricted Stock units, sign-on bonus, and other potential future incentives. Further note that total compensation for this position will be determined by each individual’s relevant qualifications, work experience, skills, and other factors.
